Individual ticket prices start at $40. Front row \(VIP\), options start at $65. Find showtimes and more details at thenewmooncircus.com. Early booking is encouraged for this highly anticipated event.

title: Nov & Dec Artwalks: "Moments in the Light"  Plein Air Painting
description:
Plein Air painting is painting on location responding to the environment as it moves you. For us it’s not about the details or exact characteristics of a location but rather the interaction of color, the atmosphere, the feeling of standing out there. It's about the immediate moment of seeing which is in the brushwork of several of the artists, creating a dialogue with the space as you make the marks and see how they correspond to what's in front of you. There is no right or wrong because it is a very personal moment. It's not impressionism. It's not quite expressionism. But it's the immediacy of being alive. 

Most of the paintings were done when Barry convinced one of the other artists to come painting with him. Creating a synergy from the overlapping influence on each other while keeping a distinct POV.

title: Winter Wonder Lantern Walks
description:
Celebrate the beauty and quiet magic of the season during Winter Wonder Lantern Walks, a festive after-dark experience at Sonoma Botanical Garden. Guided along the route by Garden staff and volunteers, guests will stroll through the winter landscape carrying glowing lanterns, discovering softly shadowed pathways, towering trees, and the peaceful stillness of the Garden beneath the night sky. Rather than a traditional docent-led tour, this experience is designed as a peaceful and immersive opportunity to enjoy the rare experience of walking through the Garden after hours and after dark. Along the way, enjoy moments of reflection, seasonal ambiance, and the simple joy of gathering outdoors during the holiday season.

The evening begins with hot cocoa, spiced cider, wine tasting and cookies from 5:30–6:00 p.m., followed by a brief welcome and lantern walk orientation before departing together for a guided walk through the Garden.

Winter Wonder Lantern Walks are a seasonal fundraiser that will support the Garden’s programs, collections, and conservation efforts. PLEASE READ the important accessibility and experience information, along with the registration and cancellation policy below before purchasing tickets.

description:
The Occidental Community Choir puts on live concerts featuring an eclectic mix of locally composed music, classical and contemporary choral pieces, poetry, and spoken word from our community in the redwoods of Northern California.

This season, "When I Rise Up," will remind us that hope is not passive, justice is not someone else's work, and the future is something that we create together. We'll explore songs of joy, hope, resilience, justice, and protest. Some of our programming will challenge us to confront difficult truths and some of it will remind us that even in times of division, compassion, courage, and community can light the way forward.

We don't answer those questions all at once. We endeavor to answer it by the choices we make, by the people we stand beside, and by the hope we refuse to surrender.

Join the Occidental Community Choir this winter for an evening of music that aims to bring a little more light into this world.

title: Meet Me in St. Louis
description: Meet Me in St. Louis is a heartwarming, nostalgic musical that brings the charm and excitement of turn-of-the-century America to life. Set in 1904 on the eve of the St. Louis World’s Fair, the story follows the Smith family through a year of romance, humor, and unexpected change. At its center is the spirited and lovestruck Esther Smith, whose blossoming romance unfolds alongside her sisters’ own adventures and the family’s hopes for the future. Featuring beloved songs like “The Trolley Song,” “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” and “The Boy Next Door,” this classic musical overflows with warmth, wit, and unforgettable melodies. Rich with period detail, lively ensemble numbers, and tender family moments, Meet Me in St. Louis celebrates community, resilience, and the enduring power of home. Audiences will be swept up in its colorful seasonal settings—from summer dances to a magical Christmas Eve—culminating in the dazzling anticipation of the World’s Fair. Perfect for theatregoers of all ages, this timeless musical offers romance, laughter, and a joyful reminder that even in times of change, love and family light the way forward. MEET ME IN ST. LOUIS is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Tams-Witmark LLC. concordtheatricals.com

This holiday season, Spreckels Theatre Company offers a heartwarming alternative to traditional seasonal fare with *Rooted*, a story about the messy, fierce love that keeps us grounded. An intelligent, gentle comedy by Deborah Zoe Laufer, *Rooted* plays Nov. 27 – Dec.13!

Emery is perfectly content living in her beloved treehouse, completely isolated from the world, communing with her plants. Meanwhile, down on the ground, her sister Hazel is thoroughly miserable, slaving away at a dead-end diner job just to survive and financially support Emery’s eccentric lifestyle. Looking on from the sidelines, Luanne is yearning for something, anything to bring true meaning into her life.

﻿The sisters' fragile ecosystem is completely upended when Emery’s YouTube videos documenting her plant experiments unexpectedly go viral. Almost overnight, her digital musings accidentally incite a full-blown CULT(!). As throngs of devoted truth-seekers congregate below the treehouse, the lives of all three women are plunged into chaos, compelling each woman to choose their own path and find their bliss.

title: David Luning
description:
John Prine forced David Luning to drop out of college. Not at gunpoint or anything—the two had never even met—but the effect of hearing the songwriting legend's music for the first time had an equally compelling effect on Luning, who was studying film scoring at the Berklee College of Music in Boston at the time. Now an accomplished artist in his own right, Luning is preparing to release his most dynamic and gripping collection to date, 'Restless,' and he can trace it all back to one fateful night that changed everything.

"A couple of friends invited me over to share some songs at their apartment, and that was the first time I'd ever really listened to Americana music or folk or country or whatever you want to call it," remembers Luning. "They showed me John Prine, and it just resonated with me so much. I was like, 'Oh my god, this is what I have to do with my life.' I just figured it out in that moment."

Luning dropped out of school almost immediately, moved back to his native California, and devoted himself to songwriting and performing. He worked his way up through open mics to large festival performances, piecing together a band to flesh out his songs along the way and hitting the road to tour with a fierce determination. His self-released debut album, 'Just Drop On By,' garnered acclaim from both critics and fellow musicians alike, with country megastar Keith Urban hailing Luning's "staunch originality." Songs from the album landed numerous film and TV placements, most recently on NBC's 'Grimm,' and Luning's reputation for exhilarating live performances earned him dates with luminaries like Jackie Greene, Dave and Phil Alvin, and Elvin Bishop, along with a slew of festival performances up and down the West Coast.

If 'Just Drop On by' announced the arrival of a promising new talent, 'Restless' delivers on that potential and then some. Recorded under the guidance of engineer/producer Karl Derfler \(Tom Waits, Dave Matthews\) and with Luning's longtime live bandmates—Ben Dubin \(bass & harmonica\), Linden Reed \(drums\), and Dave Sampson \(guitar & mandolin\)—the album marks a major step forward, both sonically and emotionally.

"With the first record, I produced and engineered everything myself," explains Luning. "I'd never worked with an outside producer before, so it was nerve-racking going into the studio with Karl for the first time, but it was just a perfect fit. It was like he knew what I wanted in my music before I even did, and he could push my performances where they needed to go and really take my music to another level."

Luning and his band set up shop at the stunning Panoramic Studios in Stinson, California, crafting a darker, grittier vibe for the music and exploring a wider palette than ever before. While many of Luning's songs are inspired by the lives and stories of the men and women he's grown up with in California or met on the road, the lyrics are all filtered through his own unique perspective and reflect his remarkable personal journey. Perhaps no track fits that bill more directly than "Driftin,'" an infectious road warrior's anthem that find's Luning singing, "I wanna keep on drifting like a rambling man."

"I had so much fun on tour going from place to place and playing to new people all the time and I got into the rhythm of it all, so when it ended and we came home I wasn't ready to stop," he explains. "We pulled into Ben's house to unload our gear and I said, 'Ben, we're packing up and we're gonna go somewhere tomorrow right? We're gonna keep on going right?'"

Much of the album is uptempo and exuberant—"Almost Sounds Like Laughing" is a foot-stomping folk tune with the energy of a runaway train—but Luning shows off his remarkable depth and range on some of the record's more restrained tracks, like the slow-burning "Brother In Chains" and delicate "Gonna Forget About You," which finds him pulling his vocals back to an intimate near-whisper that conveys a world of heartache and regret. "In Hell I Am" started life as an acoustic blues on a resonator guitar before morphing into a fiery, electric rocker, while "Bet It All On Black" takes on a harder, Southern edge, with Luning repeating the mantra, "Ain't no use in holding back."

"It's essentially about a person who's kind of carefree," he says, "and they know that something might not be the best thing to do, but they're going all in with it anyway. They're just going for it, regardless of the outcome and any repercussions they might face."

If that sounds familiar, perhaps like the attitude of a man who might risk everything to drop out of school and move across the country to pursue a dream, it's no coincidence. With songs this good, it's a safe bet that a restless soul like David Luning is going to keep on traveling for a long time to come.

title: ORGONE
description:
For nearly twenty years ORGŌNE \(a universal life force, pronounced or-gōne\) has churned out gritty funk and soul recordings and toured relentlessly across the United States and Europe. Traditionally both the studio and live iterations of the band drew on a tight-knit collective of the West Coast’s finest funk and soul musicians—although founding members Sergio Rios \(guitar/engineer\) and Dan Hastie \(keyboards\) have been constant anchors. Since late 2013, Rios and Hastie have been joined by Dale Jennings \(bass\) and Sam Halterman \(drums\) to form a permanent nucleus.

ORGŌNE’s accolades are too long to list in entirety. ORGŌNE’s live show captivates audiences and packs dance floors—whether it’s on sold out headlining tours; sharing the stage with The Roots, Al Green, Sharon Jones & the Dap-Kings, and Galactic; or appearances at festivals like Bonnaroo, New Orleans Jazz Fest, High Sierra, Bear Creek, and Jam Cruise. The well-traveled band has released albums on Ubiquity, Shanachie, and Colemine Records and served as the studio band on hits like Alicia Keys’ “Teenage Love Affair” and Cee Lo Green’s Grammy-winning “Fool For You.” Critics like NPR and Jambase don’t shy away from heaping praise on a group with “irresistible funkiness and ability to transcend genre” \(LA Weekly\).

Since ORGŌNE released their album Connection on 3 Palm Records, and distributed by Colemine Records and Secretly Distribution, they have released multiple singles including their cover of “It’s My Thing”, featuring Adryon de Leon. Their second LP from 3 Palm Records was releases in 2021, Moonshadows; featuring multiple artists from the Orgone family to create a flying high blend of late 70’s California soul and funky rock.

Use code SHRRLVLR-EARLYBIRD-12121326 to claim your discount!December 12th: Introduction to Asemic WritingDecember 13th: Wabi-Sabi Ink Painting: Finding Beauty in ImperfectionClass Description: Asemic writing is the creation of marks that resemble handwriting but carry no literal meaning or readable text. It is the word before words form—the voice too distant to be understood—a universal expression without country or dialect.We’ll begin with a slideshow exploring the rich history and possibilities of asemic writing, from ancient scripts and symbols to the calligraphic line and the work of contemporary artists. From there, you’ll begin your own exploration using ink, watercolor, and a variety of tools on paper.Through guided exercises and playful experimentation, we’ll explore line, gesture, rhythm, repetition, and space. You’ll discover how asemic marks can infiltrate and transform your existing artwork or become works of art in their own right.You’ll leave with a collection of new work, fresh approaches to mark-making, and a deeper trust in your own intuition and expressive voice. My intention is to guide you beyond casual scribbling toward authentic marks—marks that arise from the heart and become uniquely your own.All levels welcome.IMPORTANT: CLICK HERE FOR THE LIST OF REQUIRED MATERIALS FOR THIS CLASS. Not all materials are provided, please see the list of request materials above. If you have any questions regarding materials, please contact your instructor: sherrie@artandpoetry.com—About the Instructor: Sherrie Lovler is a painter, poet, and teacher whose work bridges Western calligraphy and the expressive spirit of Asian brush painting. With a BA in Studio Art, she has taught for several decades at international calligraphy conferences and institutions including Ghost Ranch, Northern Arizona University, and local art centers. Her paintings explore the space between writing and image. Inspired by Asian brushwork and the Japanese aesthetic of wabi-sabi, she embraces imperfection, spontaneity, and fluid mark-making. Sumi ink, gesture, color, and asemic writing become an abstract visual language. She is the author, illustrator, and designer of the award-winning book On Softer Ground. Her latest book, Distant Voices, explores art as a collaboration with nature, poetry, and unseen influences. She participates in Sonoma County Art Trails, Art at the Source, and presented a solo exhibition at Gallery Route One in Point Reyes Station in 2025. www.artandpoetry.com

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth **Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at** ​**Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903**. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan. 

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: Belonging to Ourselves: Understanding Trauma & Building Resilience
description:
with Pawan Bareja, PhD and Diane Poole Heller

We begin life with a child’s open heart, full of trust, innocence, and pure joy. Yet, over time, the world leaves its marks. We often arrive at our meditation cushions carrying a lifetime of hidden grief, from the lingering ache of a breakup to the quiet sorrow of a loveless childhood. To protect ourselves from this attachment trauma, we build walls that close us off from the very people we wish to love.

This daylong is an invitation to return home to the pure love that is your true nature. We do not heal in isolation; we heal together. Our nervous systems are beautifully social, wired to find safety, warmth, and co-regulation in the presence of others.

If accepting love feels foreign, you can break those protective patterns. Through guided meditations, gentle reflection, and supportive group connections, we will mend broken bonds, navigate love and conflict, and rebuild our lasting resilience.

Diane will lead a practical teaching session drawing on her background in nervous-system-informed approaches to attachment, offering an embodied complement to the day’s content.

title: Carolynne Marshall
description:
**Class Description:**

Asemic writing is the creation of marks that resemble handwriting but carry no literal meaning or readable text. It is the word before words form—the voice too distant to be understood—a universal expression without country or dialect.

We’ll begin with a slideshow exploring the rich history and possibilities of asemic writing, from ancient scripts and symbols to the calligraphic line and the work of contemporary artists. From there, you’ll begin your own exploration using ink, watercolor, and a variety of tools on paper.

Through guided exercises and playful experimentation, we’ll explore line, gesture, rhythm, repetition, and space. You’ll discover how asemic marks can infiltrate and transform your existing artwork or become works of art in their own right.

You’ll leave with a collection of new work, fresh approaches to mark-making, and a deeper trust in your own intuition and expressive voice. My intention is to guide you beyond casual scribbling toward authentic marks—marks that arise from the heart and become uniquely your own.

All levels welcome.

description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Winter Magic
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  11/15/26

**DECEMBER EXHIBIT: WINTER MAGIC**

EXHIBIT DATES:  November 23– December 27, 2026

**RECEPTION/HOLIDAY OPEN HOUSE: DECEMBER 5, 2026, 11am to 6pm: Join in to meet the artists and cheer the season, the show and enjoy holiday goodies. As part of the festivities, we will host our monthly free drawing for an artwork by Ron Sumner.  The Gallery is pleased to participate again this year in the Healdsburg Chamber’s Holiday Sip & Shop – for more information: 2026 Healdsburg Holiday Sip & Shop, Eventbrite.com.**

Sonoma County artists, **Willow LaLand, Phyllis Rapp, Linda Loveland Reid, Laura Roney, Luba Stolper, Ron Sumner, Jo Tobin-Charleston, Carolyn Wilson and Gen Zorich** present **Winter Magic,** a mix of unique artistic expressions creating a magical welcome to the 2026 holiday season.  Starting with nature’s magic -the colorful painterly skies at dawn and dusk – LaLand’s “Boston Harbor” at sunrise engenders warm feelings of hope as does Roney’s “Dancing in the Snow” in the waning rays of daylight.  Stolper weaves a spell with “Whispering Elegance,” objects so real – the lace, the cherries, the vase- the viewer is drawn in awe.  Wilson’s “New Beginnings” draws the viewer’s eye with lively colorful flowers that seem to dance for joy.  Artists Rapp and Sumner turn to our feline and feathered friends for inspiration:  in Rapp’s “Emerald Eye,” the kitty captivates us with a mesmerizing gaze and Sumner’s “Snowy Owl” looks out from its perch in a moonlit snowy glen.   From our abstract artists, Reid lights our spirit with “Green for Joy” and Zorich’s “Layers and Red Rock, “compelling in texture with splashes of random color shapes. To enable us to cast one’s own spell, Tobin-Charleston’s sparkle/colored-themed crystal pendant sets are the perfect ticket.

All member artists are showing many smaller works throughout the Gallery, ideal for gifting.

For the Holiday Season our **Staircase Showcase** features many different hand-crafted 3D artist offerings. Ceramic artists Kathy Brown, Joann Cassady, Ed Price, Karen Norton and Steve Sanders offer a variety of vases, platters, and bowls.  Our glass artists, Brian & Nancy Roberts, Melissa McCann and Tim Montesouti present gorgeous fused glass art, decorative boxes, and tree ornaments. Plus, we have horsehair bowls and decorated gourds by Susan Miron and wooden bird sculptures presented by Amber Biocca. And, as always, there is jewelry throughout the gallery. You can find the perfect earrings, necklace, pendant or bracelet from our local jewelers: Galley-member Jo Tobin-Charleston, Aaron Poovey, Laura Buckner, Melissa McCann, Patricia Reilly, Hamida Judith Dides, Elaine Greene, Heyoka Merrifield, and JoAnna Noble.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Saturdays
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? You’ve mastered the basics, now it’s time to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

**What You’ll Learn**

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

**• The Cross Body Lead (CBL) Series:** Master both **Inside and Outside Turns**, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

**• The “I Turn – You Turn”:** A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

**• The Walk-Through:** Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

**• Footwork & Shine:** We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

**Technique & Artistry**

Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

**• The Frame:** Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

**• Upper Body Mechanics:** Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

**• Connection:** Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

**Important Details**

**• No dance experience required:** Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

**• No partner necessary:** Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

title: Weekend Santa Sightings
description:
Celebrate the holidays and join us at the Village for photos with Santa happening on weekends from Saturday, November 28th to Sunday, December 20th, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. daily.

Appointments are highly recommended, as we cannot guarantee that we can accommodate all walk-ups throughout the event series. Reserve your 5-minute window now for a $35 fee during our initial release \(through Friday, November 13\). Beginning Saturday, November 14, the fee increases to $45. Each family will receive a print to take home that day, as well as a digital copy of their photo following the appointment. Please note that we do not call or text waitlisted guests.\*

Make the most of your Santa visit:

Your photo package includes up to five digital photos, emailed the Monday following your appointment, plus a print to take home that day.

Enjoy writing letters to Santa and dropping them off at the official Montgomery Village Santa Mail mailbox, plus crafts at our holiday craft tables.

Sweeten your visit! Stop by Salt & Straw before or after your appointment and enjoy a complimentary kids’ scoop with any ice cream purchase during Weekend Santa Sightings \(valid each Saturday and Sunday from 11/28/26 to 12/20/26 between 11 a.m. to 3 p.m.\).

Keep an eye out for ME SPA’s elves, spreading holiday cheer and a little stress relief with special cards to redeem at the spa. Bring yours in for a Chill Bag, a holiday survival kit filled with goodies and coupons to help you keep your cool all season long. For an extra moment of relaxation, enjoy a complimentary chair massage as scheduling allows.

Retro Foto will be assisting in making this memory last a lifetime by providing Santa with a vintage ride for all to enjoy! Retro Foto is Sonoma County’s boutique photo booth experience. Lola is a fully restored 1970 Volkswagen bus that loves the camera – whether it’s as a photo booth or a photo backdrop! Lola is all about making memories, which is why Santa thought this would be the perfect way to drive into the Holiday season!

By attending this event, guests consent to appear in photo/video recordings that may be used for website photography or other purposes.

\*A portion of proceeds will benefit Sonoma County Secret Santa Program.

title: Meet Me in St. Louis
description: Meet Me in St. Louis is a heartwarming, nostalgic musical that brings the charm and excitement of turn-of-the-century America to life. Set in 1904 on the eve of the St. Louis World’s Fair, the story follows the Smith family through a year of romance, humor, and unexpected change. At its center is the spirited and lovestruck Esther Smith, whose blossoming romance unfolds alongside her sisters’ own adventures and the family’s hopes for the future. Featuring beloved songs like “The Trolley Song,” “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” and “The Boy Next Door,” this classic musical overflows with warmth, wit, and unforgettable melodies. Rich with period detail, lively ensemble numbers, and tender family moments, Meet Me in St. Louis celebrates community, resilience, and the enduring power of home. Audiences will be swept up in its colorful seasonal settings—from summer dances to a magical Christmas Eve—culminating in the dazzling anticipation of the World’s Fair. Perfect for theatregoers of all ages, this timeless musical offers romance, laughter, and a joyful reminder that even in times of change, love and family light the way forward. MEET ME IN ST. LOUIS is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Tams-Witmark LLC. concordtheatricals.com

Sonoma, CA— November 27 - Dec 27 – This 2026 winter season, New Moon Circus invites audiences to ‘La Lune Brille’ — memorable family fun and stunning artistry under the intimate and charming atmosphere of the ‘petite’ big top.

Meet the Winter moon and her frenemy, the Sun.  When the moon is pushed from the sky, she must find a way home to the stars. Come along the journey as she encounters mysterious beings and friendly creatures on the way.

A child pleasing origin myth told through impressive aerialists, jugglers, acrobats, and clever comedy, this show blends classic storybook atmosphere with celestial magic. La Lune Brille will surprise, dazzle and delight all ages.

Spectators for all showings are invited to the European style circus tent to experience the magic up to 30 minutes before each show. Cornerstone Sonoma will provide light concession and libations for purchase. 

The event will include a 15 minute intermission during the 1 and a half hour show.

Limited free parking is available at the location at Cornerstone Sonoma.

Tickets for La Lune Brille are now available for purchase online at thenewmooncircus.com.

Individual ticket prices start at $40. Front row \(VIP\), options start at $65. Find showtimes and more details at thenewmooncircus.com. Early booking is encouraged for this highly anticipated event.

In MovingWriting workshops, we play with movement/dance and words to help us connect with our deep and creative selves in the company of a supportive circle. Giving voice to our own stories and witnessing the stories of others brings healing, aliveness, and connection with others.

No moving or writing experience necessary!

Here's what a few recent MovingWriting participants had to say about their experience:

“Loretta's well-crafted writing prompts sparked a writer inside me that I didn't know I had… I left feeling invigorated, accomplished and proud of myself for trying something new.”

“I'm neither a writer nor a dancer, but Loretta made it easy to put aside my inhibitions and let my emotional body lead the way… I recommend this class for anybody at all!”

"It felt delicious to dive into my creative moving and language self with others. For days after, I felt both emptied and filled up creatively in ways that I hadn’t felt in a long time."

"I felt refreshed, renewed, and like I had processed some emotional blockages… The paths were opened and the words just flowed."

title: Callie Watts

description: Callie Watts is a singer/songwriter from Northern California who was raised on classical music, The Beatles and The Beach Boys before discovering Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, Carole King, and all the great writers of the ’60s and 70’s who have influenced her sound and writing style. After graduating high school, Callie began playing and performing solo, as well as in local and bay area bands of different genres. She’s played blues with Eric Lindell and the Reds, funky soul with Phatty, and jazz/swing with Savoy Swingers along with many other various projects. Callie has taken turns throughout her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, and lead/backing vocalist, and she’s currently a member of the dynamic Sonoma County funk rock band Burrows and Dilbeck, having joined in 2010 as part of the former band Frobeck. Over time, she’s had the honor of opening for acts such as Bootsy Collins, Elvin Bishop, Huey Lewis and The News, War, Ozomatli, Bill Champlin, Booker T, and the B52s. Callie continues to perform frequently as an acoustic solo artist, focusing on developing a core audience and a buzz for her original material. Come hang out and listen at venues such as Aroma Roasters, Rincon Valley Tap Room and Bottle Shop, and Hopmonk Tavern.

title: Winter Wonder Lantern Walks
description:
Celebrate the beauty and quiet magic of the season during Winter Wonder Lantern Walks, a festive after-dark experience at Sonoma Botanical Garden. Guided along the route by Garden staff and volunteers, guests will stroll through the winter landscape carrying glowing lanterns, discovering softly shadowed pathways, towering trees, and the peaceful stillness of the Garden beneath the night sky. Rather than a traditional docent-led tour, this experience is designed as a peaceful and immersive opportunity to enjoy the rare experience of walking through the Garden after hours and after dark. Along the way, enjoy moments of reflection, seasonal ambiance, and the simple joy of gathering outdoors during the holiday season.

The evening begins with hot cocoa, spiced cider, wine tasting and cookies from 5:30–6:00 p.m., followed by a brief welcome and lantern walk orientation before departing together for a guided walk through the Garden.

Winter Wonder Lantern Walks are a seasonal fundraiser that will support the Garden’s programs, collections, and conservation efforts. PLEASE READ the important accessibility and experience information, along with the registration and cancellation policy below before purchasing tickets.

description:
Join us at 6 pm on SATURDAY, DECEMBER 12 for another FRIGHT NIGHT author event with readings, Q&A, and signings.

This time we're featuring CAMERON PIERCE in conversation with DAVID AGRANOFF for an evening of bizarro literature. With Ross E. Lockhart moderating, it's sure to be a fascinating discussion.

Cameron Pierce's new novel *Most Things Haven't Worked Out*, just published by CLASH Books, is a coming of age story about the painful pursuit of love, fortune, and fame reading like an optimistic Jesus' Son for a new generation. Told through a series of follies, Pierce presents a journey of finding agency from someone who doesn't have an inkling of what they want out of life.

David Agranoff's latest CLASH novel, *The Last Night to Kill Nazis*, is an emotional rollercoaster of adventure, terror and revenge that explores one of the world's most evil events through the lens of a horror novel. An entertaining and enlightening novel that is *Inglorious Basterds* meets *Dracula*. Watch for the sequel *The Next Night to Kill Nazis* coming in January!

This holiday season, Spreckels Theatre Company offers a heartwarming alternative to traditional seasonal fare with *Rooted*, a story about the messy, fierce love that keeps us grounded. An intelligent, gentle comedy by Deborah Zoe Laufer, *Rooted* plays Nov. 27 – Dec.13!

Emery is perfectly content living in her beloved treehouse, completely isolated from the world, communing with her plants. Meanwhile, down on the ground, her sister Hazel is thoroughly miserable, slaving away at a dead-end diner job just to survive and financially support Emery’s eccentric lifestyle. Looking on from the sidelines, Luanne is yearning for something, anything to bring true meaning into her life.

﻿The sisters' fragile ecosystem is completely upended when Emery’s YouTube videos documenting her plant experiments unexpectedly go viral. Almost overnight, her digital musings accidentally incite a full-blown CULT(!). As throngs of devoted truth-seekers congregate below the treehouse, the lives of all three women are plunged into chaos, compelling each woman to choose their own path and find their bliss.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

Use code SHRRLVLR-EARLYBIRD-12121326 to claim your discount!December 12th: Introduction to Asemic WritingDecember 13th: Wabi-Sabi Ink Painting: Finding Beauty in ImperfectionClass Description: Step into a creative space where intuition leads and imperfection becomes beauty. This immersive workshop explores abstract painting through both Eastern and Western perspectives, blending meditation, movement, and mark-making to create expressive, finished paintings.Rooted in the Japanese aesthetic of wabi-sabi, we’ll release the desire for perfection and welcome the unexpected. Discover the quiet magic that happens when ink meets water, gestures emerge without planning, and the body and breath guide the brush.We’ll begin with gentle centering and meditation, preparing you to work from the heart and engage your whole body in the creative process. You’ll practice painting the ensō—the Zen circle expressing wholeness, presence, movement, and stillness. Using Asian brushes, ink, and watercolor on paper, you will create calligraphic paintings with layered accents that bring depth, atmosphere, and emotion to your work.Through guided exercises and open-ended exploration, you’ll learn to trust your intuition, loosen up, and respond to what unfolds. You’ll leave with a collection of expressive paintings and new ways to bring spontaneity and freedom into your artwork.All levels welcome.IMPORTANT: CLICK HERE FOR THE LIST OF REQUIRED MATERIALS FOR THIS CLASS. If you have any questions regarding materials, please contact your instructor: sherrie@artandpoetry.com—About the Instructor: Sherrie Lovler is a painter, poet, and teacher whose work bridges Western calligraphy and the expressive spirit of Asian brush painting. With a BA in Studio Art, she has taught for several decades at international calligraphy conferences and institutions including Ghost Ranch, Northern Arizona University, and local art centers. Her paintings explore the space between writing and image. Inspired by Asian brushwork and the Japanese aesthetic of wabi-sabi, she embraces imperfection, spontaneity, and fluid mark-making. Sumi ink, gesture, color, and asemic writing become an abstract visual language. She is the author, illustrator, and designer of the award-winning book On Softer Ground. Her latest book, Distant Voices, explores art as a collaboration with nature, poetry, and unseen influences. Overeaters Anonymous \(OA\) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person meetings at 9:30 on Sunday mornings at Church of the Nazarene, 18980 Arnold Drive, Sonoma, CA \(a small room directly off of parking lot; look for the sign posted\) and newcomers are always welcome.

You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

OA is not a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does not endorse any specific food plan.

description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Intimacy with Life: Undoing the Habits That Armor the Heart with Tara Brach
description:
with James Baraz, MA, Tara Brach, PhD and Jill White Lindsay

Join us for a day of meditation and inquiry devoted to loosening the habits that separate us from our inner life and from each other. As our hearts open, we may rediscover our capacity for joy, deepen our sense of kinship with all beings, and engage more actively in caring for our world.

Jill White Lindsay will be guiding us in simple stretches and movement to ground us in our bodies as we go through the day.

title: Maple Magic & Winter Wonder
description:
As the days grow shorter and cooler, Sonoma Botanical Garden transforms with the beauty of the changing seasons. From the first signs of autumn in October to the brilliant display of rare Asian maples in November and the quiet beauty of early winter in December, each visit offers something new to discover. 

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. Throughout the season, the Garden offers guided walks, hands-on workshops, lectures, and special experiences inspired by the changing landscape. Wander among vibrant fall foliage, breathe in the sweet fragrance of katsura trees, enjoy creative programs, and experience the peaceful beauty of the Garden as it transitions into winter.

title: Stuffed and Decorate Vessels with Vicki Assegued
description:
***Class Description:***

You’ll create a free-form multi-fabric textile, then turn it into a vessel shape, stuff it, and add a vast array of wonderful fiber and decorative elements to make a super unique and fun piece of art. No art experience is necessary, and all levels are most welcome. This class is perfect for beginning through experienced students.

Please bring: Sewing needle and thread, Fabric Scissors (If you have them)

Optional: You’re encouraged to bring materials from your own stash including fabrics, used clothing, yarn, string, lace, ribbon, beads, old jewelry parts and other decorations.

title: Ultra Textural Weaving with a Unique Substrate
description:
You’ll learn many techniques for weaving, knotting, wrapping, tying, sewing, coiling and twisting of fiber materials to build our dynamic and stunning pieces to hang on the wall.

The surprising and versatile foundation for the weaving is plastic fencing, which opens the creative journey into much more than ordinary weaving.

You'll have access to plastic fencing, many gorgeous fabrics and yarns, beads, buttons and other decorations to add to your piece.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Winter Magic
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  11/15/26

**DECEMBER EXHIBIT: WINTER MAGIC**

EXHIBIT DATES:  November 23– December 27, 2026

**RECEPTION/HOLIDAY OPEN HOUSE: DECEMBER 5, 2026, 11am to 6pm: Join in to meet the artists and cheer the season, the show and enjoy holiday goodies. As part of the festivities, we will host our monthly free drawing for an artwork by Ron Sumner.  The Gallery is pleased to participate again this year in the Healdsburg Chamber’s Holiday Sip & Shop – for more information: 2026 Healdsburg Holiday Sip & Shop, Eventbrite.com.**

Sonoma County artists, **Willow LaLand, Phyllis Rapp, Linda Loveland Reid, Laura Roney, Luba Stolper, Ron Sumner, Jo Tobin-Charleston, Carolyn Wilson and Gen Zorich** present **Winter Magic,** a mix of unique artistic expressions creating a magical welcome to the 2026 holiday season.  Starting with nature’s magic -the colorful painterly skies at dawn and dusk – LaLand’s “Boston Harbor” at sunrise engenders warm feelings of hope as does Roney’s “Dancing in the Snow” in the waning rays of daylight.  Stolper weaves a spell with “Whispering Elegance,” objects so real – the lace, the cherries, the vase- the viewer is drawn in awe.  Wilson’s “New Beginnings” draws the viewer’s eye with lively colorful flowers that seem to dance for joy.  Artists Rapp and Sumner turn to our feline and feathered friends for inspiration:  in Rapp’s “Emerald Eye,” the kitty captivates us with a mesmerizing gaze and Sumner’s “Snowy Owl” looks out from its perch in a moonlit snowy glen.   From our abstract artists, Reid lights our spirit with “Green for Joy” and Zorich’s “Layers and Red Rock, “compelling in texture with splashes of random color shapes. To enable us to cast one’s own spell, Tobin-Charleston’s sparkle/colored-themed crystal pendant sets are the perfect ticket.

All member artists are showing many smaller works throughout the Gallery, ideal for gifting.

For the Holiday Season our **Staircase Showcase** features many different hand-crafted 3D artist offerings. Ceramic artists Kathy Brown, Joann Cassady, Ed Price, Karen Norton and Steve Sanders offer a variety of vases, platters, and bowls.  Our glass artists, Brian & Nancy Roberts, Melissa McCann and Tim Montesouti present gorgeous fused glass art, decorative boxes, and tree ornaments. Plus, we have horsehair bowls and decorated gourds by Susan Miron and wooden bird sculptures presented by Amber Biocca. And, as always, there is jewelry throughout the gallery. You can find the perfect earrings, necklace, pendant or bracelet from our local jewelers: Galley-member Jo Tobin-Charleston, Aaron Poovey, Laura Buckner, Melissa McCann, Patricia Reilly, Hamida Judith Dides, Elaine Greene, Heyoka Merrifield, and JoAnna Noble.

**JOIN US for ARTNITE HEALDSBURG, THURSDAY, DECEMBER 3  5:00 – 7:00 pm** : Artnite Healdsburg is a community event celebrating art and creativity with more than 20 galleries participating, along with select restaurants, bars and boutiques. 

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm; extended holiday hours: Open Fri & Sat 10am – 7pm through December 23rd; closed December 25.    **www.upstairsartgallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: FSVAA 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show
description:
2026 Juried Art Exhibit: Celebrating Northern California’s Artistic Excellence!

FSVAA proudly presents the 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show at the Solano Town Center Gallery – show opening is Friday, Nov 13. Gallery Hours are Wed thru Sun, 11am–6pm.

 The three jurors, Ferdinanda Florence, Nadja Fitchhorn, and Vickie Marchand have spoken and made their selections!

We received 200 art entries from 67 talented artists representing 15 different cities throughout Northern California, making this an exciting and impressive year for our Juried Art Show.

It was wonderful to see so many artists arrive with their treasured works of art, eager to have them reviewed and considered by our three distinguished jurors.

After careful deliberation, the jurors selected 97 outstanding works of art to be included in this year's Juried Art Show!

Congratulations to all the artists whose work was selected, and thank you to everyone who participated and helped make this year's show such a success.

EXHIBIT INFORMATION \(Save the Dates\):

• Art Show Reception /Awards Gala: Saturday, Dec 5, 2026, 3–5pm

• Reception /Poetry Reading: Saturday, Dec 19, 2026, 3–5pm

• Juror's Talk: Sunday, Jan 3, 2027, 1–3pm at the Solano Town Center Gallery  – Come hear our Jurors speak! Join us as they share their insights into the selection process, discuss what goes into choosing artwork for a juried exhibition, and offer a glimpse into their experience. As always, there will be time for a Q&A, so bring your questions!

title: Weekend Santa Sightings
description:
Celebrate the holidays and join us at the Village for photos with Santa happening on weekends from Saturday, November 28th to Sunday, December 20th, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. daily.

Appointments are highly recommended, as we cannot guarantee that we can accommodate all walk-ups throughout the event series. Reserve your 5-minute window now for a $35 fee during our initial release \(through Friday, November 13\). Beginning Saturday, November 14, the fee increases to $45. Each family will receive a print to take home that day, as well as a digital copy of their photo following the appointment. Please note that we do not call or text waitlisted guests.\*

Make the most of your Santa visit:

Your photo package includes up to five digital photos, emailed the Monday following your appointment, plus a print to take home that day.

Enjoy writing letters to Santa and dropping them off at the official Montgomery Village Santa Mail mailbox, plus crafts at our holiday craft tables.

Sweeten your visit! Stop by Salt & Straw before or after your appointment and enjoy a complimentary kids’ scoop with any ice cream purchase during Weekend Santa Sightings \(valid each Saturday and Sunday from 11/28/26 to 12/20/26 between 11 a.m. to 3 p.m.\).

Keep an eye out for ME SPA’s elves, spreading holiday cheer and a little stress relief with special cards to redeem at the spa. Bring yours in for a Chill Bag, a holiday survival kit filled with goodies and coupons to help you keep your cool all season long. For an extra moment of relaxation, enjoy a complimentary chair massage as scheduling allows.

Retro Foto will be assisting in making this memory last a lifetime by providing Santa with a vintage ride for all to enjoy! Retro Foto is Sonoma County’s boutique photo booth experience. Lola is a fully restored 1970 Volkswagen bus that loves the camera – whether it’s as a photo booth or a photo backdrop! Lola is all about making memories, which is why Santa thought this would be the perfect way to drive into the Holiday season!

By attending this event, guests consent to appear in photo/video recordings that may be used for website photography or other purposes.

\*A portion of proceeds will benefit Sonoma County Secret Santa Program.

title: New Moon Circus Presents ‘La Lune Brille
location: CORNERSTONE SONOMA - Under the Big Top Tent
description:
New Moon Circus Presents ‘La Lune Brille’: a highly original, all-human circus that enchants through breathtaking acrobatics and athletically stunning skill.

Sonoma, CA— November 27 - Dec 27 – This 2026 winter season, New Moon Circus invites audiences to ‘La Lune Brille’ — memorable family fun and stunning artistry under the intimate and charming atmosphere of the ‘petite’ big top.

Meet the Winter moon and her frenemy, the Sun.  When the moon is pushed from the sky, she must find a way home to the stars. Come along the journey as she encounters mysterious beings and friendly creatures on the way.

A child pleasing origin myth told through impressive aerialists, jugglers, acrobats, and clever comedy, this show blends classic storybook atmosphere with celestial magic. La Lune Brille will surprise, dazzle and delight all ages.

Spectators for all showings are invited to the European style circus tent to experience the magic up to 30 minutes before each show. Cornerstone Sonoma will provide light concession and libations for purchase. 

The event will include a 15 minute intermission during the 1 and a half hour show.

Limited free parking is available at the location at Cornerstone Sonoma.

Tickets for La Lune Brille are now available for purchase online at thenewmooncircus.com.

Individual ticket prices start at $40. Front row \(VIP\), options start at $65. Find showtimes and more details at thenewmooncircus.com. Early booking is encouraged for this highly anticipated event.

Annual Lucia Jul Fika with Linnea Lodge
description:
Come celebrate Scandinavian holiday traditions with Linnea Lodge!

Linnea Lodge \#504 invites Members, families, friends, and those interested in Scandinavian holiday traditions to come participate in our annual Lucia Jul Fika.

A Swedish "fika" is a break in the day to enjoy coffee and a treat. We're taking fika and adding our annual Santa Lucia pageant and other Jul traditions for a day of cultural fellowship. Enjoy live music, dancing around the tree, a gift basket drawing, and a special visit from Jultomten \(Santa!\) to complete the festivities.\*\*

Coffee, tea, and soft drinks will be served, along with sandwiches, cheese and crackerbread, fruit, cookies, and traditional Swedish lussekatter \(saffron buns\).

What to bring:

- Members: Please bring 1 small Poinsettia for tables and a dozen cookies or a baked treat for our Fika

- \*\*For everyone bringing children, please bring a small wrapped gift for each child in your party with their name printed clearly on the package. \(Drop off packages discretely at check in.\)

Children participating in the pageant are asked to arrive at 1:30 PM for practice. Participating boys should wear black pants and a white shirt. Gowns provided.

Seating is limited. Please RSVP by December 2nd.

title: Meet Me in St. Louis
description: Meet Me in St. Louis is a heartwarming, nostalgic musical that brings the charm and excitement of turn-of-the-century America to life. Set in 1904 on the eve of the St. Louis World’s Fair, the story follows the Smith family through a year of romance, humor, and unexpected change. At its center is the spirited and lovestruck Esther Smith, whose blossoming romance unfolds alongside her sisters’ own adventures and the family’s hopes for the future. Featuring beloved songs like “The Trolley Song,” “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” and “The Boy Next Door,” this classic musical overflows with warmth, wit, and unforgettable melodies. Rich with period detail, lively ensemble numbers, and tender family moments, Meet Me in St. Louis celebrates community, resilience, and the enduring power of home. Audiences will be swept up in its colorful seasonal settings—from summer dances to a magical Christmas Eve—culminating in the dazzling anticipation of the World’s Fair. Perfect for theatregoers of all ages, this timeless musical offers romance, laughter, and a joyful reminder that even in times of change, love and family light the way forward. MEET ME IN ST. LOUIS is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Tams-Witmark LLC. concordtheatricals.com

location: Spreckels Center for the Performing Arts - Bette Condiotti Experimental Theatre
description:
This holiday season, Spreckels Theatre Company offers a heartwarming alternative to traditional seasonal fare with *Rooted*, a story about the messy, fierce love that keeps us grounded. An intelligent, gentle comedy by Deborah Zoe Laufer, *Rooted* plays Nov. 27 – Dec.13!

Emery is perfectly content living in her beloved treehouse, completely isolated from the world, communing with her plants. Meanwhile, down on the ground, her sister Hazel is thoroughly miserable, slaving away at a dead-end diner job just to survive and financially support Emery’s eccentric lifestyle. Looking on from the sidelines, Luanne is yearning for something, anything to bring true meaning into her life.

﻿The sisters' fragile ecosystem is completely upended when Emery’s YouTube videos documenting her plant experiments unexpectedly go viral. Almost overnight, her digital musings accidentally incite a full-blown CULT(!). As throngs of devoted truth-seekers congregate below the treehouse, the lives of all three women are plunged into chaos, compelling each woman to choose their own path and find their bliss.

description:
The Occidental Community Choir puts on live concerts featuring an eclectic mix of locally composed music, classical and contemporary choral pieces, poetry, and spoken word from our community in the redwoods of Northern California.

This season, "When I Rise Up," will remind us that hope is not passive, justice is not someone else's work, and the future is something that we create together. We'll explore songs of joy, hope, resilience, justice, and protest. Some of our programming will challenge us to confront difficult truths and some of it will remind us that even in times of division, compassion, courage, and community can light the way forward.

description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

title: Focus Night: Geminids Meteor Shower
description: Move over, summer Perseids. December's Geminid shower is considered the best and most reliable meteor shower of the year. Under dark clear skies, counts can reach 50-100 per hour or more on peak night. But this is only one of many factors that set these meteors apart from all other showers. Their speed and composition create meteors that flare low in the atmosphere, are easier to spot, and leave bright, often yellow, trails. This is one of the very few showers visible all night long. What causes this dazzling display and why does it occur at this time of year? Come learn about these unique meteors, their unusual history, and their mysterious origin. This Focus Night equips you for a Geminid ”peak” experience. Unlike planets that can hang around for months, a meteor shower is only visible over a short period of time. Highest counts will occur later in the night and into the early morning hours. You will learn about different kinds of showers, how best to view them, and how to understand what you are seeing. You’ll also discover factors that influence meteor counts and how to optimize your viewing. Plan to be in the classroom by 6:55PM to ensure you have a good seat. Program begins promptly at 7:00PM . Sales are limited to 40 guests so we can provide a more personal experience. Allow generous time to arrive and park. Please visit https://rfo.simpletix.com for important information and to buy tickets. You MUST have a ticket to attend this event; tickets will not be sold at the door. Cost includes the Sugarloaf Ridge State Park parking fee. Please note that tickets are non-refundable and cannot be used for future events.RFO is operated by the Valley of the Moon Observatory Association, a 501(3)(c) nonprofit organization. All proceeds go toward maintaining this beloved Sonoma County institution.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Art Exhibit: Winter Magic
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  11/15/26

**DECEMBER EXHIBIT: WINTER MAGIC**

EXHIBIT DATES:  November 23– December 27, 2026

**RECEPTION/HOLIDAY OPEN HOUSE: DECEMBER 5, 2026, 11am to 6pm: Join in to meet the artists and cheer the season, the show and enjoy holiday goodies. As part of the festivities, we will host our monthly free drawing for an artwork by Ron Sumner.  The Gallery is pleased to participate again this year in the Healdsburg Chamber’s Holiday Sip & Shop – for more information: 2026 Healdsburg Holiday Sip & Shop, Eventbrite.com.**

Sonoma County artists, **Willow LaLand, Phyllis Rapp, Linda Loveland Reid, Laura Roney, Luba Stolper, Ron Sumner, Jo Tobin-Charleston, Carolyn Wilson and Gen Zorich** present **Winter Magic,** a mix of unique artistic expressions creating a magical welcome to the 2026 holiday season.  Starting with nature’s magic -the colorful painterly skies at dawn and dusk – LaLand’s “Boston Harbor” at sunrise engenders warm feelings of hope as does Roney’s “Dancing in the Snow” in the waning rays of daylight.  Stolper weaves a spell with “Whispering Elegance,” objects so real – the lace, the cherries, the vase- the viewer is drawn in awe.  Wilson’s “New Beginnings” draws the viewer’s eye with lively colorful flowers that seem to dance for joy.  Artists Rapp and Sumner turn to our feline and feathered friends for inspiration:  in Rapp’s “Emerald Eye,” the kitty captivates us with a mesmerizing gaze and Sumner’s “Snowy Owl” looks out from its perch in a moonlit snowy glen.   From our abstract artists, Reid lights our spirit with “Green for Joy” and Zorich’s “Layers and Red Rock, “compelling in texture with splashes of random color shapes. To enable us to cast one’s own spell, Tobin-Charleston’s sparkle/colored-themed crystal pendant sets are the perfect ticket.

All member artists are showing many smaller works throughout the Gallery, ideal for gifting.

For the Holiday Season our **Staircase Showcase** features many different hand-crafted 3D artist offerings. Ceramic artists Kathy Brown, Joann Cassady, Ed Price, Karen Norton and Steve Sanders offer a variety of vases, platters, and bowls.  Our glass artists, Brian & Nancy Roberts, Melissa McCann and Tim Montesouti present gorgeous fused glass art, decorative boxes, and tree ornaments. Plus, we have horsehair bowls and decorated gourds by Susan Miron and wooden bird sculptures presented by Amber Biocca. And, as always, there is jewelry throughout the gallery. You can find the perfect earrings, necklace, pendant or bracelet from our local jewelers: Galley-member Jo Tobin-Charleston, Aaron Poovey, Laura Buckner, Melissa McCann, Patricia Reilly, Hamida Judith Dides, Elaine Greene, Heyoka Merrifield, and JoAnna Noble.

You’ll develop coordination, body awareness, strength, and confidence while learning to move with greater ease and expression.

No previous dance experience is required. All bodies and experience levels are welcome.

Come move to the music, connect with your body, and discover the joy of bellydancing

CAREM LOVE

Carem Love is a wellness advocate, professional dancer, and certified yoga instructor with a Bachelor’s degree in Dance. She has extensive training in Bellydance, a deep passion for Latin dance, and is certified in Hatha, Vinyasa, and Children’s Yoga.

Belly dance has profoundly supported her health, well-being, and dance career, inspiring her to help others experience the same body-mind benefits. In her classes, students learn to connect more deeply with themselves.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Mondays
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

Date & Time:

Monday 6:00 PM

Saturday 11:00 AM

Instructor: Lucie Ebnerova

Address: 4140 Redwood Highway \#8 San Rafael, CA \(salsa lessons in Marin\)

Note: Arrive 10 minutes before. No floor marking shoe soles allowed.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Discovering Women Poets, a Poetry Competition
description:
The National League of American Pen Women (NLAPW) and the Golden Gate-Marin Branch are launching a poetry competition for women over 18 years of age who are not currently members of the NLAPW. This regional and national competition will be run at the Branch level in the semi-finalist phase. Local winners are automatically entered into the League’s National competition.

Winners at the Branch level will receive $35 and have their entry published in the Branch newsletter. They will also be invited to present their poetry in person or by Zoom.

Branch winners become semi-finalists in the National competition, which will award $100 to three winners. National winners will have their work and a short bio published in The Pen Woman, a national magazine. All semi-finalists will be listed in the magazine.

Up to three poems may be submitted for one entry fee of $15. Each poem should be no longer than 40 lines. There are no restrictions on topics or poem’s structure. Entries must be received by January 25, 2027.

Download Entry Form at our website: https://www.goldengatemarinart.org/copy-of-contact

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Maple Magic & Winter Wonder
description:

From the first signs of autumn in October to the brilliant display of rare Asian maples in November and the quiet beauty of early winter in December, each visit offers something new to discover. 

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. Throughout the season, the Garden offers guided walks, hands-on workshops, lectures, and special experiences inspired by the changing landscape. Wander among vibrant fall foliage, breathe in the sweet fragrance of katsura trees, enjoy creative programs, and experience the peaceful beauty of the Garden as it transitions into winter.

title: Belly Dancing with Raja - Tuesdays
description:
DATE AND TIME: Tuesdays @ 11:00 AM

Unlock your inner strength and find your flow. Belly dancing with Raja is an innovative fusion class that blends the rhythmic artistry of belly dance with the high-energy benefits of aerobics. Designed to be both a cardiovascular challenge and a deep toning session, this class focuses on the “powerhouse” of the body—your core.

By layering fluid, isolative movements over an athletic aerobic base, you will challenge your muscles in ways traditional gym workouts can’t reach.

What to Expect in Belly Dancing Class

• Core-Centric Power: Use undulations and shimmies to engage deep abdominal muscles for a tighter, stronger midsection.

• Functional Stability: Improve your balance and posture through controlled, hip-driven movements and low-impact aerobic footwork.

• Total Body Toning: Build lean muscle in your legs, glutes, and arms while maintaining a constant, heart-pumping pace.

• Mind-Body Connection: Enhance your coordination and body awareness through rhythmic, expressive choreography.

“Whether you’re looking to define your waistline or simply want a workout that feels like a celebration, this class offers the perfect balance of sweat and grace.”

Difficulty Level: All levels welcome! No prior dance experience is required—just bring your energy and a willingness to move.
