title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

title: Discovering Women Poets, a Poetry Competition
description:
The National League of American Pen Women (NLAPW) and the Golden Gate-Marin Branch are launching a poetry competition for women over 18 years of age who are not currently members of the NLAPW. This regional and national competition will be run at the Branch level in the semi-finalist phase. Local winners are automatically entered into the League’s National competition.

Winners at the Branch level will receive $35 and have their entry published in the Branch newsletter. They will also be invited to present their poetry in person or by Zoom.

Branch winners become semi-finalists in the National competition, which will award $100 to three winners. National winners will have their work and a short bio published in The Pen Woman, a national magazine. All semi-finalists will be listed in the magazine.

Up to three poems may be submitted for one entry fee of $15. Each poem should be no longer than 40 lines. There are no restrictions on topics or poem’s structure. Entries must be received by January 25, 2027.

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Life Reimagined: Art, Healing & Connection
description:
Life Reimagined is a supportive, community-based workshop that brings together individuals whose lives have been touched by cancer, whether currently navigating treatment, in recovery, or living beyond a cancer diagnosis and are interested in exploring the role art has played in their lives.

This workshop will encourage an open dialogue and hands-on art projects to enrich the group experience. We will celebrate creativity, honor our resilience, and support each other on our artistic journeys.

A $5 materials fee will be collected at the beginning of class.

About Cathryn Hudin 

Cathryn is an accomplished, professional ceramic artist whose distinguished career spans several decades. She has served as an instructor and President of Board of Directors at Paradise Art Center and has taught ceramics at Butte College and California State University, Chico. Through her participation in the Artists-in-Schools Program, she has shared her passion for art with students and inspired the next generation of artists. A cancer survivor, Cathryn embodies resilience and perseverance, qualities that inform her life, her work and her endearing commitment to the arts.

title: Maple Magic & Winter Wonder
description:
As the days grow shorter and cooler, Sonoma Botanical Garden transforms with the beauty of the changing seasons. From the first signs of autumn in October to the brilliant display of rare Asian maples in November and the quiet beauty of early winter in December, each visit offers something new to discover. 

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. Throughout the season, the Garden offers guided walks, hands-on workshops, lectures, and special experiences inspired by the changing landscape. Wander among vibrant fall foliage, breathe in the sweet fragrance of katsura trees, enjoy creative programs, and experience the peaceful beauty of the Garden as it transitions into winter.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Winter Magic
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  11/15/26

**DECEMBER EXHIBIT: WINTER MAGIC**

EXHIBIT DATES:  November 23– December 27, 2026

**RECEPTION/HOLIDAY OPEN HOUSE: DECEMBER 5, 2026, 11am to 6pm: Join in to meet the artists and cheer the season, the show and enjoy holiday goodies. As part of the festivities, we will host our monthly free drawing for an artwork by Ron Sumner.  The Gallery is pleased to participate again this year in the Healdsburg Chamber’s Holiday Sip & Shop – for more information: 2026 Healdsburg Holiday Sip & Shop, Eventbrite.com.**

Sonoma County artists, **Willow LaLand, Phyllis Rapp, Linda Loveland Reid, Laura Roney, Luba Stolper, Ron Sumner, Jo Tobin-Charleston, Carolyn Wilson and Gen Zorich** present **Winter Magic,** a mix of unique artistic expressions creating a magical welcome to the 2026 holiday season.  Starting with nature’s magic -the colorful painterly skies at dawn and dusk – LaLand’s “Boston Harbor” at sunrise engenders warm feelings of hope as does Roney’s “Dancing in the Snow” in the waning rays of daylight.  Stolper weaves a spell with “Whispering Elegance,” objects so real – the lace, the cherries, the vase- the viewer is drawn in awe.  Wilson’s “New Beginnings” draws the viewer’s eye with lively colorful flowers that seem to dance for joy.  Artists Rapp and Sumner turn to our feline and feathered friends for inspiration:  in Rapp’s “Emerald Eye,” the kitty captivates us with a mesmerizing gaze and Sumner’s “Snowy Owl” looks out from its perch in a moonlit snowy glen.   From our abstract artists, Reid lights our spirit with “Green for Joy” and Zorich’s “Layers and Red Rock, “compelling in texture with splashes of random color shapes. To enable us to cast one’s own spell, Tobin-Charleston’s sparkle/colored-themed crystal pendant sets are the perfect ticket.

All member artists are showing many smaller works throughout the Gallery, ideal for gifting.

For the Holiday Season our **Staircase Showcase** features many different hand-crafted 3D artist offerings. Ceramic artists Kathy Brown, Joann Cassady, Ed Price, Karen Norton and Steve Sanders offer a variety of vases, platters, and bowls.  Our glass artists, Brian & Nancy Roberts, Melissa McCann and Tim Montesouti present gorgeous fused glass art, decorative boxes, and tree ornaments. Plus, we have horsehair bowls and decorated gourds by Susan Miron and wooden bird sculptures presented by Amber Biocca. And, as always, there is jewelry throughout the gallery. You can find the perfect earrings, necklace, pendant or bracelet from our local jewelers: Galley-member Jo Tobin-Charleston, Aaron Poovey, Laura Buckner, Melissa McCann, Patricia Reilly, Hamida Judith Dides, Elaine Greene, Heyoka Merrifield, and JoAnna Noble.

**JOIN US for ARTNITE HEALDSBURG, THURSDAY, DECEMBER 3  5:00 – 7:00 pm** : Artnite Healdsburg is a community event celebrating art and creativity with more than 20 galleries participating, along with select restaurants, bars and boutiques. 

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm; extended holiday hours: Open Fri & Sat 10am – 7pm through December 23rd; closed December 25.    **www.upstairsartgallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: FSVAA 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show
description:
2026 Juried Art Exhibit: Celebrating Northern California’s Artistic Excellence!

FSVAA proudly presents the 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show at the Solano Town Center Gallery – show opening is Friday, Nov 13. Gallery Hours are Wed thru Sun, 11am–6pm.

 The three jurors, Ferdinanda Florence, Nadja Fitchhorn, and Vickie Marchand have spoken and made their selections!

We received 200 art entries from 67 talented artists representing 15 different cities throughout Northern California, making this an exciting and impressive year for our Juried Art Show.

It was wonderful to see so many artists arrive with their treasured works of art, eager to have them reviewed and considered by our three distinguished jurors.

After careful deliberation, the jurors selected 97 outstanding works of art to be included in this year's Juried Art Show!

Congratulations to all the artists whose work was selected, and thank you to everyone who participated and helped make this year's show such a success.

EXHIBIT INFORMATION \(Save the Dates\):

• Art Show Reception /Awards Gala: Saturday, Dec 5, 2026, 3–5pm

• Reception /Poetry Reading: Saturday, Dec 19, 2026, 3–5pm

• Juror's Talk: Sunday, Jan 3, 2027, 1–3pm at the Solano Town Center Gallery  – Come hear our Jurors speak! Join us as they share their insights into the selection process, discuss what goes into choosing artwork for a juried exhibition, and offer a glimpse into their experience. As always, there will be time for a Q&A, so bring your questions!

title: Chris Shiflett
description: Alt-country songwriter. Rock & roll guitarist. Pop-punk pioneer. Chris Shiflett has played multiple roles during his 20\+ year career, fronting his own band one minute and serving as the Foo Fighters' longtime guitarist the next. He turns a new corner with West Coast Town, an autobiographical solo album that finds Shiflett pulling triple-duty as singer, songwriter and bandleader.   Heavily inspired by both the unique twang of California's country tradition — particularly Bakersfield icons like Buck Owens and Merle Haggard —  and the rootsy stomp of the Rolling Stones, West Coast Town is an extension of the acclaimed alt-country career Shiflett kickstarted back in 2010. It's a bright, bold album, with Shiflett revising the supposed "rules" of country music to suit his own background. There are no songs about Georgia back roads here. No southern belles in denim cut-offs. Instead, Shiflett — a California native who grew up in Santa Barbara — writes about an adolescence spent onstage, on the beach, and on the prowl. During the nostalgic title track, "West Coast Town," a teenage Shiflett chases girls along the Pacific Ocean shoreline, returning home at night to his childhood home on Salinas Street. Later, he drinks away an ex's memory in "Room 102," battles hangovers and heartbreak in "I'm Still Drunk," and triumphantly wraps up a rock & roll show with "Goodnight Little Rock."  "'Goodnight Little Rock' is a truck driving country song," he says of the rowdy, guitar-driven track, "but written from the viewpoint of a van tour. That's as close as I've come to ever being a truck driver."   Truck driver or not, Shiflett has spent the past two decades crisscrossing the globe, playing thousands of shows along the way. In 2016, those travels took him to Nashville, where he interviewed Grammy-winning producer Dave Cobb as part of his weekly podcast, Walking the Floor with Chris Shiflett. The meeting took place at RCA Studio A, shortly after Cobb moved his recording operations into the historic room. There, surrounded by vintage gear and the ghosts of country music's greatest singers, Cobb and Shiflett formed a genuine friendship. "When I left the studio," Shiflett remembers, "I thought, 'I have to make a record with that dude.' I was already a big fan of the records Cobb produces, and his setup was just so amazing."  Later that summer, Shiflett came back to Nashville, this time with a catalog of new songs in tow. West Coast Town, his first solo album since 2013's collection of honky-tonk covers, All Hat and No Cattle, was recorded at RCA Studio A over a three-week period, with help from Grammy-winning engineer/mixer Matt Ross-Spang. Cobb doubled as the album's producer and acoustic guitar player, with a group of A-list studio musicians — pedal steel guitarist Robby Turner \(Waylon Jennings, Chris Stapleton\), drummer Chris Powell \(Brent Cobb, Jamey Johnson\), bassist Adam Gardner \(Southern Family\), and keyboardist Michael Webb \(Southern Family\) — adding their own contributions. On an album filled with all-star names, though, Shiflett plays the biggest role, singing and picking his way through 10 original songs that mix together the bounce of Bakersfield country, the anthemic punch of blue-collar roots-rock, the rule-breaking rebelliousness of SoCal punk, and plenty of guitar heroics.   With every song captured in two or three takes, West Coast Town often sounds more like the work of a live band than a studio creation. That approach suits the songs well. After all, this is an album about growing up — about making peace with your roots — and growing up is always a bit messy. Asked about his influences, Shiflett rattles off names like the Stray Cats, Social Distortion, Dwight Yoakam, and Uncle Tupelo, all of whom challenged the rules of the genres they occupied. West Coast Town follows a similar path. Although set in coastal California, it's an album that creates its own geography — a place where dark lyrics rub shoulders with bright bursts of melody; where country music doesn't just belong to American South, where the soft swoon of pedal steel makes way for sharply-worded lyrics; and where one of modern music's biggest multi-taskers can combine his songwriting, singing and guitar-playing talents into one track list. title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Discovering Women Poets, a Poetry Competition
description:
The National League of American Pen Women (NLAPW) and the Golden Gate-Marin Branch are launching a poetry competition for women over 18 years of age who are not currently members of the NLAPW. This regional and national competition will be run at the Branch level in the semi-finalist phase. Local winners are automatically entered into the League’s National competition.

Winners at the Branch level will receive $35 and have their entry published in the Branch newsletter. They will also be invited to present their poetry in person or by Zoom.

Branch winners become semi-finalists in the National competition, which will award $100 to three winners. National winners will have their work and a short bio published in The Pen Woman, a national magazine. All semi-finalists will be listed in the magazine.

Up to three poems may be submitted for one entry fee of $15. Each poem should be no longer than 40 lines. There are no restrictions on topics or poem’s structure. Entries must be received by January 25, 2027.

Download Entry Form at our website: https://www.goldengatemarinart.org/copy-of-contact

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Winter Magic
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  11/15/26

**DECEMBER EXHIBIT: WINTER MAGIC**

EXHIBIT DATES:  November 23– December 27, 2026

**RECEPTION/HOLIDAY OPEN HOUSE: DECEMBER 5, 2026, 11am to 6pm: Join in to meet the artists and cheer the season, the show and enjoy holiday goodies. As part of the festivities, we will host our monthly free drawing for an artwork by Ron Sumner.  The Gallery is pleased to participate again this year in the Healdsburg Chamber’s Holiday Sip & Shop – for more information: 2026 Healdsburg Holiday Sip & Shop, Eventbrite.com.**

Sonoma County artists, **Willow LaLand, Phyllis Rapp, Linda Loveland Reid, Laura Roney, Luba Stolper, Ron Sumner, Jo Tobin-Charleston, Carolyn Wilson and Gen Zorich** present **Winter Magic,** a mix of unique artistic expressions creating a magical welcome to the 2026 holiday season.  Starting with nature’s magic -the colorful painterly skies at dawn and dusk – LaLand’s “Boston Harbor” at sunrise engenders warm feelings of hope as does Roney’s “Dancing in the Snow” in the waning rays of daylight.  Stolper weaves a spell with “Whispering Elegance,” objects so real – the lace, the cherries, the vase- the viewer is drawn in awe.  Wilson’s “New Beginnings” draws the viewer’s eye with lively colorful flowers that seem to dance for joy.  Artists Rapp and Sumner turn to our feline and feathered friends for inspiration:  in Rapp’s “Emerald Eye,” the kitty captivates us with a mesmerizing gaze and Sumner’s “Snowy Owl” looks out from its perch in a moonlit snowy glen.   From our abstract artists, Reid lights our spirit with “Green for Joy” and Zorich’s “Layers and Red Rock, “compelling in texture with splashes of random color shapes. To enable us to cast one’s own spell, Tobin-Charleston’s sparkle/colored-themed crystal pendant sets are the perfect ticket.

All member artists are showing many smaller works throughout the Gallery, ideal for gifting.

For the Holiday Season our **Staircase Showcase** features many different hand-crafted 3D artist offerings. Ceramic artists Kathy Brown, Joann Cassady, Ed Price, Karen Norton and Steve Sanders offer a variety of vases, platters, and bowls.  Our glass artists, Brian & Nancy Roberts, Melissa McCann and Tim Montesouti present gorgeous fused glass art, decorative boxes, and tree ornaments. Plus, we have horsehair bowls and decorated gourds by Susan Miron and wooden bird sculptures presented by Amber Biocca. And, as always, there is jewelry throughout the gallery. You can find the perfect earrings, necklace, pendant or bracelet from our local jewelers: Galley-member Jo Tobin-Charleston, Aaron Poovey, Laura Buckner, Melissa McCann, Patricia Reilly, Hamida Judith Dides, Elaine Greene, Heyoka Merrifield, and JoAnna Noble.

**JOIN US for ARTNITE HEALDSBURG, THURSDAY, DECEMBER 3  5:00 – 7:00 pm** : Artnite Healdsburg is a community event celebrating art and creativity with more than 20 galleries participating, along with select restaurants, bars and boutiques. 

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm; extended holiday hours: Open Fri & Sat 10am – 7pm through December 23rd; closed December 25.    **www.upstairsartgallery.net**

title: FSVAA 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show

FSVAA proudly presents the 63rd Annual Nor-Cal Regional Juried Art Show at the Solano Town Center Gallery – show opening is Friday, Nov 13. Gallery Hours are Wed thru Sun, 11am–6pm.

 The three jurors, Ferdinanda Florence, Nadja Fitchhorn, and Vickie Marchand have spoken and made their selections!

We received 200 art entries from 67 talented artists representing 15 different cities throughout Northern California, making this an exciting and impressive year for our Juried Art Show.

It was wonderful to see so many artists arrive with their treasured works of art, eager to have them reviewed and considered by our three distinguished jurors.

After careful deliberation, the jurors selected 97 outstanding works of art to be included in this year's Juried Art Show!

Congratulations to all the artists whose work was selected, and thank you to everyone who participated and helped make this year's show such a success.

title: Bachata Beginners Thursday
description:
Your First Steps into Bachata

This class is perfect for bachata beginners that want to learn basic steps and skills, or those who want to refresh their foundational skills. We understand that learning something new can feel a little intimidating. That’s why our supportive and relaxed environment is specifically designed to make learning bachata basics an absolute blast!

Our friendly instructors will guide you through:

**Basic directional steps:** You’ll learn the fundamental movements that form the building blocks of all bachata dancing.

**Proper frame for partner work:** Discover how to connect comfortably and effectively with a partner, setting you up for smooth and enjoyable dances.

**Simple turn patterns:** We’ll introduce you to easy-to-follow turn patterns that will have you dancing with a partner in no time.

We’ve carefully organized our curriculum to ensure that each movement is easy to grasp and remember, building your confidence with every step. Our goal is to make learning fun. Join us to learn Bachata in Marin.

Important Details

**No dance experience required:** Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

**No partner necessary:** Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

Please wear **non-marking shoe soles:** This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

Come join us and discover the joy of bachata! We can’t wait to see you on the dance floor.

title: Gain Speaking Confidence with Mare Island Toastmasters
description:
We meet in-person only on the 1st and 2nd Thursdays of the month. However, you can catch us online every Thursday unless the meeting date falls on a holiday.

Please register at https://signup.com/go/WiniixA

What is Toastmasters About?

Usually at our meetings, we will have a prepared speech, and a speech evaluation. The Grammarian and Wizard of Ah's will listen for turns of phrases and the use of filler words. We also practice impromptu speaking during the section of the meeting called Table Topics. During Table Topics, at a recent meeting, we were asked what we felt was the biggest communication problem or challenge. What would you answer in a fast moment? Table topics will challenge you to think quickly and give an answer without preparation.

You will also hear tips on public speaking skills at our upcoming meeting. Whether you're a seasoned traveler or just looking for some adventure from the comfort of your home, this event is perfect for you.

Toastmasters International is all about communication excellence, and for 100 years and counting, Toastmasters have been expressing themselves better, practicing, and evaluating in a fun club environment, shining all around the world.

To find out more--Msg us on our webpage \(under Contact Us\) button at

https://mareisland.toastmastersclubs.org/

If you will join us in-person on the first or second Thursday of the month, we meet this week at Kaiser Hospital Bldg. A. 3rd floor meeting room. When you enter the hospital building, go past the piano to the elevator. Go to the 3rd floor. Exit left out of the elevator and left at the hall. Go past the gym and take a left at the hall. Walk down the long hall to the meeting room.

title: Join Mare Island Toastmasters and Learn Speaking Tips and Tricks
description:
Do you want to learn some tips to improve your communication skills? Will you give a speech at an upcoming meeting or event? Toastmasters can help. Please join us weekly online \(except holidays\). We only have a hybrid meeting \(in-person and online only the 1st and 2nd Thursdays of the month.

Join us for a fun filled, fast paced meeting at 7:30pm Pacific Time.

Toastmasters can:

1. help you communicate with confidence,

2. help you improve listening skills,

3. help improve your feedback skills, and

4. improve your impromptu speaking skills, and more.

The 3 main parts to the meeting are:

\*\*Prepared Speech

title: Shawn Jones
description:
Shawn Jones: Bio

Shawn Jones is the epitome of American Roots/Rock music. He has proven over time that he has an international appeal. He is true to form of his influences, spanning from all the greats in Rock, Rhythm & Blues, Jazz & Country. His father raised him on Hank Williams, and he grew up in the outskirts of Los Angeles, where he learned from experience how to play and sing the blues. Since his late teens, Shawn has been working away, at times in excess of 200 dates a year, creating new fans and followers literally everywhere he performs. With three studio albums and one live album under his belt, Shawn’s skills as a seasoned songwriter, guitarist, and vocalist have put him on the same bill with the likes of BB King, Buddy Guy, Bonnie Raitt, Jimmie Vaughan, Willie Nelson, Leon Russell, Eric Johnson, Robben Ford, Derek Trucks, Little Feat, Joe Bonamassa, David Lindley, and others. Waylon Jennings was also so impressed with his live performance that he took Jones under his wing, offering him the grand opportunity to play on his 1996 release "Right For The Time."  Shawn was also Waylon's lead guitarist on Lollapalooza, and Willie's 4th of July Picnic. Shawn’s third album, appropriately titled, “All In Good Time," was completed in the fall of 2005 with Grammy winning producer/engineer David Z. In 2007 he played on country artist Deana Carter’s Vanguard Records release "The Chain", and to this day tours with her as her guitarist. 

Currently, Shawn is in the studio, working on his fifth album due out Summer, 2011.

He's also been creating quite a buzz overseas, touring extensively in the U.K. and Ireland at some of the major music festivals, collecting rave reviews. He has appeared on BBC Northern Ireland, and U105 FM where his music has found a new home getting airplay. Back in the States, Shawn’s song “Invincible Me” was featured in the 100th episode of “Dawson’s Creek” on the Fox Network. Jones and his band made a cameo appearance in the Fine Line Pictures release,“Tumbleweeds”, starring Golden Globe winning actress, Janet McTeer. Two of his songs, “Long Way Down” and “Lightening Strike Me Down” are featured in the movie. The single “Long Way Down” was also included on the RCA/Victor soundtrack album. Other artists on the album include: Johnny Cash, Lyle Lovett, Buck Owens, Emmylou Harris and Lucinda Williams. Shawn’s song “Lightening Strike Me Down” was selected for the Hollywood Pictures film, “Mystery Alaska” starring Russell Crowe.

Shawn Jones' ability to combine undeniable guitar playing, singing, writing, and recording, coupled with heartfelt emotion, has earned him the slot as one of the most compelling new artists on today’s roots music scene.

 

And the wheels roll on . . .

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

Black students are invited to submit original artwork in any medium or theme, including visual art, poetry, and other forms of creative writing. Artwork does not need to focus on Black identity or the Black experience—the exhibition celebrates the breadth of Black creativity and the individuality of each participating artist.  The exhibition will be on display in the ground floor library display cases from the beginning of the Spring 2027 semester through Spring Break. Students interested in participating must drop off their work at the SRJC Multicultural Museum by December 18, 2026.Learn more about the museum on the SRJC Multicultural Museum website. description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Art Exhibit: Winter Magic
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  11/15/26

**DECEMBER EXHIBIT: WINTER MAGIC**

EXHIBIT DATES:  November 23– December 27, 2026

**RECEPTION/HOLIDAY OPEN HOUSE: DECEMBER 5, 2026, 11am to 6pm: Join in to meet the artists and cheer the season, the show and enjoy holiday goodies. As part of the festivities, we will host our monthly free drawing for an artwork by Ron Sumner.  The Gallery is pleased to participate again this year in the Healdsburg Chamber’s Holiday Sip & Shop – for more information: 2026 Healdsburg Holiday Sip & Shop, Eventbrite.com.**

Sonoma County artists, **Willow LaLand, Phyllis Rapp, Linda Loveland Reid, Laura Roney, Luba Stolper, Ron Sumner, Jo Tobin-Charleston, Carolyn Wilson and Gen Zorich** present **Winter Magic,** a mix of unique artistic expressions creating a magical welcome to the 2026 holiday season.  Starting with nature’s magic -the colorful painterly skies at dawn and dusk – LaLand’s “Boston Harbor” at sunrise engenders warm feelings of hope as does Roney’s “Dancing in the Snow” in the waning rays of daylight.  Stolper weaves a spell with “Whispering Elegance,” objects so real – the lace, the cherries, the vase- the viewer is drawn in awe.  Wilson’s “New Beginnings” draws the viewer’s eye with lively colorful flowers that seem to dance for joy.  Artists Rapp and Sumner turn to our feline and feathered friends for inspiration:  in Rapp’s “Emerald Eye,” the kitty captivates us with a mesmerizing gaze and Sumner’s “Snowy Owl” looks out from its perch in a moonlit snowy glen.   From our abstract artists, Reid lights our spirit with “Green for Joy” and Zorich’s “Layers and Red Rock, “compelling in texture with splashes of random color shapes. To enable us to cast one’s own spell, Tobin-Charleston’s sparkle/colored-themed crystal pendant sets are the perfect ticket.

All member artists are showing many smaller works throughout the Gallery, ideal for gifting.

For the Holiday Season our **Staircase Showcase** features many different hand-crafted 3D artist offerings. Ceramic artists Kathy Brown, Joann Cassady, Ed Price, Karen Norton and Steve Sanders offer a variety of vases, platters, and bowls.  Our glass artists, Brian & Nancy Roberts, Melissa McCann and Tim Montesouti present gorgeous fused glass art, decorative boxes, and tree ornaments. Plus, we have horsehair bowls and decorated gourds by Susan Miron and wooden bird sculptures presented by Amber Biocca. And, as always, there is jewelry throughout the gallery. You can find the perfect earrings, necklace, pendant or bracelet from our local jewelers: Galley-member Jo Tobin-Charleston, Aaron Poovey, Laura Buckner, Melissa McCann, Patricia Reilly, Hamida Judith Dides, Elaine Greene, Heyoka Merrifield, and JoAnna Noble.

**JOIN US for ARTNITE HEALDSBURG, THURSDAY, DECEMBER 3  5:00 – 7:00 pm** : Artnite Healdsburg is a community event celebrating art and creativity with more than 20 galleries participating, along with select restaurants, bars and boutiques. 

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm; extended holiday hours: Open Fri & Sat 10am – 7pm through December 23rd; closed December 25.    **www.upstairsartgallery.net**

Some people find it useful to bring a journal or sketchbook as part of their looking tools. Some basic art materials will be available.

title: Callie Watts
description: Callie Watts is a singer/songwriter from Northern California who was raised on classical music, The Beatles and The Beach Boys before discovering Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, Carole King, and all the great writers of the ’60s and 70’s who have influenced her sound and writing style. After graduating high school, Callie began playing and performing solo, as well as in local and bay area bands of different genres. She’s played blues with Eric Lindell and the Reds, funky soul with Phatty, and jazz/swing with Savoy Swingers along with many other various projects. Callie has taken turns throughout her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, and lead/backing vocalist, and she’s currently a member of the dynamic Sonoma County funk rock band Burrows and Dilbeck, having joined in 2010 as part of the former band Frobeck. Over time, she’s had the honor of opening for acts such as Bootsy Collins, Elvin Bishop, Huey Lewis and The News, War, Ozomatli, Bill Champlin, Booker T, and the B52s. Callie continues to perform frequently as an acoustic solo artist, focusing on developing a core audience and a buzz for her original material. \- A professional female magician, Ari Rose Magic, bringing captivating spellwork to life as Auntie Drosselmeyer!

\- Community Legends: A special guest appearance by the owners of Taylor Dance (formerly Nordquist Dance), performing as Clara’s parents and bringing a custom ballroom flair to the Party Scene!

From exquisite choreography and lavish costumes to Tchaikovsky’s iconic score, it’s an extraordinarily rich, family-friendly holiday experience!

title: Fr. Brendan Williams - Poems/Prayers
description: Father Brendan Williams, chaplain of Bishop's Ranch outside Healdsburg, in conversation with Denise Low. The intersections of prayer and poetry are shared inspirations from religious traditions for both of these poets. They will talk about biblical and other religious texts as subliminal cultural guides as well as deliberate choices they make in their respective practices. Psalms and hymns have long influenced sonnets and today's short lyrical poems. Ginsberg's Kaddish is an audacious example of intertextual borrowing from Jewish tradition. Williams is a priest, spiritual director, yogi, healer, scholar, and teacher of religion. His work spans Western and Eastern esoterica, indigenous Gaelic lifeways, meditation, and contemplative spirituality. He chants old rebel tales, traces the song-streams of ancient wisdom, and ferries souls along the mythic riverways of human transformation-guiding people from all walks of life back to their birthright of wholeness and freedom within the great ecology of spirit.

title: Meet Me in St. Louis
description: Meet Me in St. Louis is a heartwarming, nostalgic musical that brings the charm and excitement of turn-of-the-century America to life. Set in 1904 on the eve of the St. Louis World’s Fair, the story follows the Smith family through a year of romance, humor, and unexpected change. At its center is the spirited and lovestruck Esther Smith, whose blossoming romance unfolds alongside her sisters’ own adventures and the family’s hopes for the future. Featuring beloved songs like “The Trolley Song,” “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” and “The Boy Next Door,” this classic musical overflows with warmth, wit, and unforgettable melodies. Rich with period detail, lively ensemble numbers, and tender family moments, Meet Me in St. Louis celebrates community, resilience, and the enduring power of home. Audiences will be swept up in its colorful seasonal settings—from summer dances to a magical Christmas Eve—culminating in the dazzling anticipation of the World’s Fair. Perfect for theatregoers of all ages, this timeless musical offers romance, laughter, and a joyful reminder that even in times of change, love and family light the way forward. MEET ME IN ST. LOUIS is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Tams-Witmark LLC. concordtheatricals.com

title: Bella Rayne
description:
MEET BELLA RAYNE | GUITARIST

18 year old Bella Rayne is a self-taught guitarist, vocalist, and songwriter, born in the mountains of North Carolina and raised in coastal Mendocino, California, whose bold blend of jam band energy, Southern-tinged rock, ’90s grunge grit, and psychedelic spirit is rapidly capturing attention across the U.S. 

Her journey began during the pandemic, when boredom led her to resurrect an old Stratocaster she found in her garage. She fixed it up, learned to play by ear, and quickly found her voice — melding influences from rock, Americana, bluegrass, and the jam-band legacy into something deeply her own.                                              

Despite her young age, Bella has already shared the stage with seasoned artists and respected bands. Appearances alongside Allman Betts Family Revival, Melvin Seals & JGB, ALO, Jackie Greene, Oteil Burbridge, and members of Terrapin Family have all added to her early résumé PLUS she was touted as “one to watch” by her idol, Susan Tedeschi in Guitar World Magazine.

One of the most iconic moments of her rising career: she was entrusted to play the legendary guitar known as “Alligator” — once wielded by Jerry Garcia. That honor, courtesy of Grateful Guitars Foundation, has become a defining chapter in Bella’s journey. 

Bella has formed her own project, Bella Rayne Band — a high-energy, guitar-driven ensemble featuring a young lineup of seasoned musicians. Their sets are a blend of soulful Southern-rock, modern Americana and Grateful Dead reinterpretations plus their own originals, earning increasing demand across venues and festivals.

With her infectious spirit, fearless originality, and genre-bending vision, Bailey Callahan is redefining what country music can be - bold, shimmering, and undeniably her own.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

description:
As the days grow shorter and cooler, Sonoma Botanical Garden transforms with the beauty of the changing seasons. From the first signs of autumn in October to the brilliant display of rare Asian maples in November and the quiet beauty of early winter in December, each visit offers something new to discover. 

*Maple Magic* *& Winter Wonder* invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. title: Meet Me in St. Louis
description: Meet Me in St. Louis is a heartwarming, nostalgic musical that brings the charm and excitement of turn-of-the-century America to life. Set in 1904 on the eve of the St. Louis World’s Fair, the story follows the Smith family through a year of romance, humor, and unexpected change. At its center is the spirited and lovestruck Esther Smith, whose blossoming romance unfolds alongside her sisters’ own adventures and the family’s hopes for the future. Featuring beloved songs like “The Trolley Song,” “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” and “The Boy Next Door,” this classic musical overflows with warmth, wit, and unforgettable melodies. Rich with period detail, lively ensemble numbers, and tender family moments, Meet Me in St. Louis celebrates community, resilience, and the enduring power of home. Audiences will be swept up in its colorful seasonal settings—from summer dances to a magical Christmas Eve—culminating in the dazzling anticipation of the World’s Fair. Perfect for theatregoers of all ages, this timeless musical offers romance, laughter, and a joyful reminder that even in times of change, love and family light the way forward. MEET ME IN ST. description:
A professional-level presentation of Tchaikovsky’s classic Nutcracker ballet with a spectacular community twist! Experience the timeless magic of the holidays with Dance Evolution Studios (formerly Santa Rosa Dance Theater)! This beloved tradition tells the enchanting story of young Clara, whose Christmas Eve dream unfolds into a world of swirling snowflakes, dancing sweets, and unforgettable adventure.

This year’s production elevates the tale with world-class talent and surprising new delights, including:

\- A professional female magician, Ari Rose Magic, bringing captivating spellwork to life as Auntie Drosselmeyer!

\- Star-Studded Guest Artists: Professional guest dancers—including former performers with Dance Theater of Harlem and San Francisco Ballet. dancing alongside the talented students of DES

\- Live Guest Musicians: Jeanette Isenberg (second violinist with the Santa Rosa Symphony) and award-winning pianist Robert Young

\- Community Legends: A special guest appearance by the owners of Taylor Dance (formerly Nordquist Dance), performing as Clara’s parents and bringing a custom ballroom flair to the Party Scene!

From exquisite choreography and lavish costumes to Tchaikovsky’s iconic score, it’s an extraordinarily rich, family-friendly holiday experience!

Elevate Your Evening with VIP Tickets: Upgrade to VIP for an exclusive backstage tour and an elegant wine-and-charcuterie spread at intermission. The perfect touch to make your Nutcracker night truly magical.

title: Yesteryear by Caro Claire Burke (option 1)
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
A modern day Christian tradwife Natalie decides with her husband to take the family to live in a farmhouse, grow their own food, raise chickens and a cow, and raise/home school their ever-increasing brood without modern influences. However -- mom is also a social media influencer who videos everything... except the nannies and farmworkers behind the scenes. She wakes up one day and she and some version of her family are in a real farmhouse (with no helpers) in 1855! How to get out of this nightmare/delusion/time travel?

"I found it to be a realy page turner--couldn't put it down. I definitely think that we should read this for our group. It's so unusual and I think it would provide fodder for very interesting discussion." - Nancy R.

"For the life of me, I can’t figure out why I kept reading this book given that most of the characters in it are deplorable. But I sure kept reading it. And then when I finished it, I wondered what kind of a person could write such a book and I was surprised when I listened to the interview that the author is actually full-fledged human being with a heart and a sense of humor. To me, that the sign of someone with tremendous craft. There are many topics in this book that I think would be a wealth for us to discuss: The double lives of social media influencers, Tradwife vs Girlboss, can we go back into the way that used to be. I suspect the reason this book is so hot because it’s so topical." - Lucinda

"It took me a bit to get into (I was just so annoyed at the beginning:) but after things began to develop, I was hooked. A lot to discuss - although it may be tough to separate out discussion on the book itself and the real-world implications!" - Debra

"[Why You Should Read ‘Yesteryear’ Now](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/10/briefing/yesteryear-caro-claire-burke.html?unlocked_article_code=1.01A.Gak9.SZGpJviEJq74&smid=url-share)" - NY Times

"‘[Yesteryear’ is this summer’s must-discuss book. We have questions.](https://www.washingtonpost.com/style/interactive/2026/06/18/yesteryear-is-this-summers-must-read-book-let-discuss/)" - Washington Post:

To register for this workshop, please contact Jan at: mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com

Creating note cards from pressed flowers has been Jan’s hobby for 25 years, though she has no formal art training. She utilizes color,
shape and texture on fine quality paper, each card uniquely handmade. Jan’s home in Sebastopol is her studio: the dining room table is her workshop, the kitchen cupboards storing boxes and trays of flowers. She buys card stock by the thousand and picks blooms from her garden and other public places. Her family is used to me saying, “could we stop for just a few minutes so I can gather some… ”

It is a wonderful way of life.

Sips and Stars ~ an evening of fine wine and cosmic wonder.

Join us for a magical night under the stars at the Robert Ferguson Observatory! Our Sips & Stars event blends the beauty of the night sky with the elegance of Sonoma County wine. Enjoy a curated tasting experience hosted by Burtech Family Vineyard,  while taking in breathtaking views of the cosmos through our powerful telescopes.

As twilight falls, relax with a glass of wine in hand and listen to engaging astronomy talks from our knowledgeable docents. Once darkness settles, step up to the observatory’s telescopes for guided viewing of planets, star clusters, and distant galaxies.

Whether you’re a wine lover, stargazer, or simply looking for a unique evening out in Sonoma Valley, Sips & Stars promises an unforgettable experience where earthly pleasures meet celestial beauty.

title: Callie Watts
description: Callie Watts is a singer/songwriter from Northern California who was raised on classical music, The Beatles and The Beach Boys before discovering Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, Carole King, and all the great writers of the ’60s and 70’s who have influenced her sound and writing style. After graduating high school, Callie began playing and performing solo, as well as in local and bay area bands of different genres. She’s played blues with Eric Lindell and the Reds, funky soul with Phatty, and jazz/swing with Savoy Swingers along with many other various projects. Callie has taken turns throughout her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, and lead/backing vocalist, and she’s currently a member of the dynamic Sonoma County funk rock band Burrows and Dilbeck, having joined in 2010 as part of the former band Frobeck. Over time, she’s had the honor of opening for acts such as Bootsy Collins, Elvin Bishop, Huey Lewis and The News, War, Ozomatli, Bill Champlin, Booker T, and the B52s. Callie continues to perform frequently as an acoustic solo artist, focusing on developing a core audience and a buzz for her original material. Come hang out and listen at venues such as Aroma Roasters, Rincon Valley Tap Room and Bottle Shop, and Hopmonk Tavern.

title: Chanting, Meditation, and Winter Solstice Ritual
description:
with Jai Uttal, Frank Ostaseski, Nubia Teixeira and Prajna Vieira

The great love, joy, and sacred light that this season celebrates are found within our own hearts. During our time together, we will use the powerful and sublime blend of chanting and meditation to carry us from the frenzy of “holiday mind” to the ocean of the awakened heart. This uplifting evening will include chanting \(call and response\) and meditation, and we will conclude with a beautiful candlelight ritual to honor the winter solstice.

Together we’ll experience the nourishment of interconnection as we practice and pray in community for the healing of our world. We’ll also share the innate joy that is uncovered when we collectively chant \(and dance, if you feel moved to do so\).

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

location: Rileystreet Art Supply, 103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:

Date: Sunday, December 20th
Time: 2:00PM-5:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Fee: $40.00

This is a hands-on make and take class where you will make at least five items including a bookmark, a greeting card, a fridge magnet and an ornament. The class will use two different techniques and Jan will explain how to press flowers and which flowers hold their color best. It is a creative experience!


To register for this workshop, please contact Jan at: mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com

Creating note cards from pressed flowers has been Jan’s hobby for 25 years, though she has no formal art training. She utilizes color,
shape and texture on fine quality paper, each card uniquely handmade. Jan’s home in Sebastopol is her studio: the dining room table is her workshop, the kitchen cupboards storing boxes and trays of flowers. She buys card stock by the thousand and picks blooms from her garden and other public places. Her family is used to me saying, “could we stop for just a few minutes so I can gather some… ”

It is a wonderful way of life.

*A note to all students: Please park on in the East facing parking lot while attending classes. We greatly appreciate it. Thank you.

description:
Poetry Lives! December 22nd!

  
    
      
      from $0.00
    
  

Every Fourth Tuesday: December 22nd, 2026 6:00-7:00pm: Spoken Word Workshop 7:15-8:30pm: Open Mic Open to All$5/10/15/20 Sliding Scale for Workshop Join us for an evening of spoken word poetry here at the Sebastopol Center for the Arts! Students of all walks of life, abilities, and experience writing poetry, or spoken word poetry, are encouraged to join. Students will engage in a freewrite, poetry reading, discussion, and structured writing with a voluntary shareout. After the one hour workshop, Poetry Lives! will act as an Open Mic night open to all to read their completed, or previously completed, poems. To register for the Open Mic only, please select Open Mic Only below! All workshop registrations include registration to the open mic as well. Poetry Lives! is a monthly poetry workshop and open mic series that aims to create a space for anyone and everyone to come, learn more about poetic craft, and share their poetry. The event starts with a facilitated hour-long workshop dedicated to learning craft elements, discovering new poets, and generating new work. Once the workshop concludes, we will hold a hosted open mic for anyone who wishes to share. It is not mandatory to participate in the workshop to be a part of the open mic or vice versa. title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Yesteryear by Caro Claire Burke (option 2)
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
A modern day Christian tradwife Natalie decides with her husband to take the family to live in a farmhouse, grow their own food, raise chickens and a cow, and raise/home school their ever-increasing brood without modern influences. However -- mom is also a social media influencer who videos everything... except the nannies and farmworkers behind the scenes. She wakes up one day and she and some version of her family are in a real farmhouse (with no helpers) in 1855! How to get out of this nightmare/delusion/time travel?

"I found it to be a realy page turner--couldn't put it down. I definitely think that we should read this for our group. It's so unusual and I think it would provide fodder for very interesting discussion." - Nancy R.

"For the life of me, I can’t figure out why I kept reading this book given that most of the characters in it are deplorable. But I sure kept reading it. And then when I finished it, I wondered what kind of a person could write such a book and I was surprised when I listened to the interview that the author is actually full-fledged human being with a heart and a sense of humor. To me, that the sign of someone with tremendous craft. There are many topics in this book that I think would be a wealth for us to discuss: The double lives of social media influencers, Tradwife vs Girlboss, can we go back into the way that used to be. I suspect the reason this book is so hot because it’s so topical." - Lucinda

"It took me a bit to get into (I was just so annoyed at the beginning:) but after things began to develop, I was hooked. A lot to discuss - although it may be tough to separate out discussion on the book itself and the real-world implications!" - Debra

"[Why You Should Read ‘Yesteryear’ Now](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/10/briefing/yesteryear-caro-claire-burke.html?unlocked_article_code=1.01A.Gak9.SZGpJviEJq74&smid=url-share)" - NY Times

"‘[Yesteryear’ is this summer’s must-discuss book. We have questions.](https://www.washingtonpost.com/style/interactive/2026/06/18/yesteryear-is-this-summers-must-read-book-let-discuss/)" - Washington Post

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

Wednesday, Ongoing

Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Poetic Medicine in Community: Healing Through Creativity and Connection: 01/05/2027 — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Poetic Medicine in Community: Healing Through Creativity and Connection: January 5th, 2027

  
    
      
        
          $15.00
        
      
    
  

Poetic Medicine in Community: Healing Through Creativity and ConnectionTuesday, January 5th, 4:00-5:30pm Class Description: Poetry can be a salve for the heart and soul. It is a way of speaking what is true in our hearts and is often difficult to access without a creative spark. You do not have to be a “poet” or even a “writer” to allow words and feeling to your through your pen. COME JOIN US!Writing poetry in community is a bit like attending a meditation retreat. The instruction for most beginners when learning to meditate is to simply bring oneself back to the breath, each time the mind wanders. In poem-making, the instruction is to bring oneself back to the heart and along with a deep breath, see if one can open a little bit wider. When we witness each other in this process, in a circle of open-heartedness, something magical happens!This is an IN-PERSON gathering in an open and safe creative community. We are all poets! Please bring your own writing materials. 22 students maximum. About the Instructor: Redwing Keyssar has been leading “Poetic Medicine in Community” sessions through her work in Palliative Care at UCSF since 2020. Her work has created an international community of people who, by listening to and writing poetry together, have healed wounds of grief and loss, helped ”wounded healers,” and provided resiliency to move forward on our life paths.Redwing is a Palliative Care nurse, educator and consultant, an end-of-life doula, author, poet, song-writer, ceremonialist, national presenter and frequent contributor to public issues about Palliative and End of Life Care. She is a Board member of the Sebastopol Senior Center and offers presentations about end-of-life issues throughout the Bay Area. Before working at the UCSF MERI CENTER, her professional career included being the Clinical Director at Zen Hospice Project and the Director of Palliative Care and Nursing at Jewish Family and Children’s Services from 2004-2018. She is a founder and adjunct faculty member of the California State University Shiley/Haynes Institute of Palliative Care and has taught courses at OLLI at Sonoma State. Redwing is the author of an award-winning book, “Last Acts of Kindness; Lessons for the Living from the Bedsides of the Dying” and is the recipient of numerous awards in the field of Palliative Care.She is passionate about utilizing poetry as a healing modality!
