title: Intro to Wheel Throwing with Naomi (6 sessions)  — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Out of Stock
      
    





Intro to Wheel Throwing with Naomi (January 2027)

  
    
      
        
          $290.00
        
      
    
  

Wednesdays, starting January 6th through February 10th (6 sessions) 2:00-5:00pm$250 + $40 Clay Fee (max 10 students)Class Description:This course is designed for students who are new to the potter’s wheel and eager to discover the fundamentals of wheel throwing. With an emphasis on core technique, each session builds a solid foundation in the essential skills of centering, opening, pulling up walls, trimming and glazing — the building blocks that every potter returns to again and again.Each class begins with a demonstration focused on one or more of these foundational techniques, giving students a clear picture of the process before getting their hands in the clay. From there, students work at their own wheels with plenty of time to practice, explore and develop their feel for the material. The goal is for each person to leave the course being able to make a thrown piece — a bowl, a mug, a vase — that is genuinely their own, shaped by their emerging skills and their personal sense of what they love about pottery.With two teachers in the room, there is ample opportunity for individual attention and hands-on guidance at every stage of the process. At the same time, there is real joy in learning alongside others — watching a classmate pull up a wall for the first time, or seeing a finished glaze come out of the kiln — and that shared experience is very much a part of what makes this class special.No prior experience is necessary. All you need is curiosity and a willingness to get a little muddy.About the Instructors: Naomi Fuchs brings a deep love of clay and a genuine passion for sharing the experience with others to everything she does in the clay room. She believes that each pot is an opportunity to learn — about the nature of clay, and about yourself. Naomi has been throwing on the wheel for four years, and in that time the practice has become a grounding, peaceful and creative part of her life that has deepened her connection to art and making. Her warm, encouraging approach creates a space where beginners feel supported as they find their footing at the wheel and begin to discover what clay can do in their hands.

Observational Drawing - 6 Week Series January 6th, 13th, 20th, 27th, February 3rd and 10th6:00-9:00pm$300.00 + $25.00 Materials Fee = $325.00 About this Class: In this six week course, students will learn and practice observational skills and fundamental drawing techniques that will inform all of their other creative pursuits. This course is for anyone who wants to practice and advance their drawing skills - beginners, those who haven’t practiced in years, or any artists who just want to learn new techniques and practice their skills with consistent feedback and guidance. Through demonstration, practice, and reflective discussion, this class will explore the foundations of classical drawing techniques in a low pressure environment. Observational drawing gives all artists a foundation of practical knowledge and skills that infinitely expands the possibilities of what one can create. If your ideas feel limited by your drawing skills, if you feel frustrated or stuck in your painting practice, or if you simply want to start drawing and are looking for a place to start, this is the class for you. About the Instructor: Hannah Day received her BA in Visual Arts with an emphasis on drawing and printmaking from University of San Diego, then attended University of Hawaii at Manoa to receive her MFA in printmaking. Hannah’s etchings have been internationally shown and collected, but her art practice also includes paper cutting, graphite, and watercolor. She has taught all ages in many mediums. These days, Hannah primarily teaches watercolor, observational drawing, and paper cutting. Wednesday, Ongoing

Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Give 'Em the Axe! Ladies Night at the Range in Santa Rosa
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
Join us for an axe-throwing session to blow off some steam. I'm super excited to be able to offer a ladies' Axe-throwing night in Santa Rosa. If you've ever had a curiosity about this fun activity, this is your chance to find out more!

We have reserved a group spot with the indoor range on a Wednesday night. It will consist of an introductory lesson, and then we all get to practice taking turns. Everyone will get ample time to practice, as they have many lanes.

This event is focused on a less-competitive, relaxed, and entertaining atmosphere. All skill levels are encouraged. All equipment and targets are provided by them, and we will probably get about 1 to 2 hours to enjoy ourselves.

I encourage everyone to bring a bottle of wine or a snack to share with the rest of the group (We usually end up with a lovely charcuterie and wine spread for everyone to enjoy).

There are 10 spots available, guests welcome. The ladies' group lesson and event is $31 per person, with $6 prepaid via Paypal and $25 paid to the range.

Please only RSVP 'Yes' if you are able to make it, hostess Daima Phipps will be collecting a $6 fee via Paypal to hold your spot. Paypal/Meetup should lead you to make your payment after you RSVP 'Yes'.

Closed-toed shoes are recommended.

There is an attendance policy for all our events: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

Cheers, and hope to see you there!

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

title: John of John by Douglas Stuart (option 1)
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
*Publisher's description*: A vivid, moving novel following a young man returning to his Hebridean island home, a portrait of a father's expectations and a son's desires.

Out of money and with little to show for his art school education, John-Calum Macleod takes the ferry back home to the Isle of Harris in the Outer Hebrides to find that little has changed except for him. He returns to the windswept croft and the two pillars of his childhood: his father John, a sheep farmer, tweed weaver, and lay preacher in the local Presbyterian church, and his maternal grandmother Ella, a profanity-loving Glaswegian whose steady warmth helped Cal weather the sudden departure of his mother.

Cal privately wonders if any lonely men might be found on the barren hillsides of home, while John is dismayed by his son's long hair, strange clothes, and seeming unwillingness to be Saved. But Cal isn't the only one who is keeping secrets. As lambing season turns to shearing season, the threads holding together the community together become increasingly frayed, and nothing will remain as it was before. *John of John* is a singular novel about duty, passion, and the transformative power of the truth.

*From our members*:

Mac: "a must-read for our Novel Lovers discussions. It contains beautiful, accurate descriptions of the harsh sere landscape in the Outer Hebrides where I’ve visited. It’s filled with secrets, many revealed and others not. Stuart dishes up human hope and despair in equal measure. Having dwelt on very different islands with small face-to-face communities like those on Harris and Lewis, the novel reflects life in many other places besides the far west of Scotland."

Matthew: "I did appreciate *John of John* and greatly admire Douglas Stuart's thoughtful writing. Sheep farming on a remote Scottish isle is a world so removed. It's very much an internal dialogue with the handful of characters, with a number ancillary family members and neighbors. I finished the book several weeks ago and it's stayed with me."

Ma'ayan: "I LOVED it all the way through. It broke my heart but also gave me hope. I laughed out loud at certain parts, too. The writing is so visceral. This one really stole my heart."

Joan: "So much in this book. It's about finding/denying/finding one's true self; keeping family secrets and secrets kept from family; passion and denial of passion; staying upright when family, religion, and the hardscrabble life of sheep farming on a Scottish island beat you down. Some books just get to you. This one gets to me."

title: Voyage Hot Club
description:
Django meets French Chanson
Award-winning violinist
Eva Slongo
, guitarist
Jimmy Grant
and Double bassist
Simon Planting
present an intimate and swinging duo rooted in the gypsy jazz tradition of
Django Reinhardt
and
Stéphane Grappelli
. Their music draws equally from European jazz, Eastern European folk influences, and classic vocal jazz, resulting in a sound that feels both timeless and accessible to modern audiences.
Their repertoire includes French chanson, swing standards, and original arrangements that evoke travel, nostalgia, and joy. Whether presented in a listening-room jazz club, concert hall, or outdoor summer series, Eva and Jimmy offer a warm, dynamic performance that emphasizes groove, melody, and connection.
Tickets for this event are $33 GA, $28 for OCA members. Doors open at 6:30 PM, refreshments available. Art Gallery open during intermission Contact us to request ADA seating,
info@occidentalcenterforthearts.org
Get Tickets
About the performers:
Jimmy Grant,
hailing from Northern California, discovered Django Reinhardt's vibrant sounds while touring with his dad’s bluegrass band. His unique style, shaped by influences like Bach and Joe Pass, was honed under the mentorship of guitarists Jim Nichols and Howard Alden.
Jimmy has performed with renowned artists such as David Grisman, Gonzalo Bergara, and many more showcasing his talent at prestigious events like Djangofest Northwest and The New York Hot Jazz Festival, as well as venues throughout the US & Europe.
As an educator, he teaches across the U.S. and hosts "Camp Django" in Ashland, OR. He contributes to "Gypsy Jazz Secrets Magazine" and has recorded two albums. His original composition "Insomnia" was a finalist in the John Lennon Songwriting Competition.
Eva Slongo
was born in Switzerland to a family of classical musicians. She first trained as a professional classical violinist.
One day, by chance, she tried to improvise with musicians in a bar; she felt such euphoria that she spent a sleepless night … It was then that she decided to do everything she could to practice improvisation on the violin.
After her classical diplomas, she changed direction and started from scratch … She studied jazz violin with Pierre Blanchard in Lausanne, then with Didier Lockwood in Paris, where she decided to stay and live for music. She also practiced improvisation on vocals, which led her to create her very noticeable unique color: improvising on the violin and scatting simultaneously.
In Paris, Eva Slongo met renowned musicians from the world of gypsy jazz with whom she shared the stage: Biréli Lagrène, Wawau Adler, Sébastien Giniaux, Ninine Garcia, and many others …
In 2011, she won the Prize for Best Improvisation at the Stéphane Grappelli International Violin Competition sponsored by Didier Lockwood. In 2016, she obtained the 2nd prize of the Golden Jazz Trophy with her quartet.
After all these years of experience, she was led to give masterclasses internationally. She needed to share more of her learning of the jazz violin, but struggled to find the time and method to do so. Her first pregnancy forced her to slow down concerts… but it led her to do what she would never have imagined: create a new educational concept on the internet, the blog “Learn Jazz Violin” which has become the 1st Google search result in French jazz violin, and finally a method “The new way to learn jazz violin.”
Eva Slongo’s new album “Souffle” was recorded in collaboration with pianist Giovanni Mirabassi, with whom she shares the stage regularly.
Dutch double bassist
Simon Planting
studied classical bass at the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra and jazz at the Sweelinck Conservatory in Amsterdam. Now based near San Francisco, he has performed internationally with artists including Mathilde Santing, Fapy Lafertin, Jimmy Rosenberg, Stephane Wrembel, and John Jorgenson, and is a fixture on the Djangofest circuit.

title: Storytelling with Brian Martens: The Story of Iron John
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Storytelling afternoon with Brian Martens: The Story of Iron John.
Join Brian for a storytelling event designed to help you become the author of your own myth and understand your place in the world. Iron John, a Grimm Bros. tale, is about the maturing of a young Prince who goes through initiations with curiosity and trust in a Wild Man. Each step on his path is a test, an opening, and an unknowing that leads him further into maturity. The surprise ending matches the mystery, revelation, and mythic consequences that an ancient tale reveals. There will be two short breaks for discussion, and a final Q&A. Refreshments will be available for sale.
Pre-registration is suggested but not necessary. $25 non-OCA members, $20 OCA members.
Get Tickets
Brian, an abstract Artist, Poet, Author, Creativity Facilitator, International Speaker, Myth Maker, CA Poets in the Schools Instructor, Podcaster, and Storyteller, weaves poetry, myth, and reflection into all his storytelling. His first book,
Three Raven Gate
, is a collection of haiku, the form he learned from his work with Angeles Arrien Ph.D., a cross-cultural anthropologist, over the course of seven years. Brian seeks to inspire and motivate people, with articles, podcasts, creativity workshops, and poetry to recognize their own deep creative spirit and to express that to the world.

title: THIRSTY THURSDAY New Member Social for Sonoma County Women's Wine Club
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
This is our regular club meeting, held on the last Thursday of every month except for holidays and we are super excited! Come join us at 4th Street Cellars in downtown Santa Rosa. They have generously offered to host our monthly THIRSTY THURSDAY social for us.

If you are new to the area, or just looking to get out of the house and make new friends, this is the place for you. Welcoming to ALL new and (ahem, old) members.

Wine is purchased by the glass for a set fee of $13/$14 per glass with the variety of white, rosé, and red wines offered through 4th Street Cellars which includes tip. Fees are collected at the venue by Co-organizer Daima Phipps via cash, Venmo, or Paypal. You are welcome to purchase wine separately if you choose. Starting in 2026, we ask that every attending member pay a $2 "slush" fund fee per event so that we can build up our funds for club-related expenses, which can be paid by Venmo or cash.

There is no food offered, but you are welcome to bring an appetizer or snack to share with the group, and many ladies do. We will have time to socialize while tasting in the room upstairs to the left or the outside patio if the weather is nice.

The space has a 25 person attendee limit, but the list is open to 40 to eliminate a waitlist, and guests are welcome! Please RSVP below only if you are able to make it, we have an attendance policy: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

See you there, ready to kickoff!

Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women. title: John of John by Douglas Stuart (option 2)
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
*Publisher's description*: A vivid, moving novel following a young man returning to his Hebridean island home, a portrait of a father's expectations and a son's desires.

Out of money and with little to show for his art school education, John-Calum Macleod takes the ferry back home to the Isle of Harris in the Outer Hebrides to find that little has changed except for him. He returns to the windswept croft and the two pillars of his childhood: his father John, a sheep farmer, tweed weaver, and lay preacher in the local Presbyterian church, and his maternal grandmother Ella, a profanity-loving Glaswegian whose steady warmth helped Cal weather the sudden departure of his mother.

Cal privately wonders if any lonely men might be found on the barren hillsides of home, while John is dismayed by his son's long hair, strange clothes, and seeming unwillingness to be Saved. But Cal isn't the only one who is keeping secrets. As lambing season turns to shearing season, the threads holding together the community together become increasingly frayed, and nothing will remain as it was before. *John of John* is a singular novel about duty, passion, and the transformative power of the truth.

*From our members*:

Mac: "a must-read for our Novel Lovers discussions. It contains beautiful, accurate descriptions of the harsh sere landscape in the Outer Hebrides where I’ve visited. It’s filled with secrets, many revealed and others not. Stuart dishes up human hope and despair in equal measure. Having dwelt on very different islands with small face-to-face communities like those on Harris and Lewis, the novel reflects life in many other places besides the far west of Scotland."

Matthew: "I did appreciate *John of John* and greatly admire Douglas Stuart's thoughtful writing. Sheep farming on a remote Scottish isle is a world so removed. It's very much an internal dialogue with the handful of characters, with a number ancillary family members and neighbors. I finished the book several weeks ago and it's stayed with me."

Ma'ayan: "I LOVED it all the way through. It broke my heart but also gave me hope. I laughed out loud at certain parts, too. The writing is so visceral. This one really stole my heart."

Joan: "So much in this book. It's about finding/denying/finding one's true self; keeping family secrets and secrets kept from family; passion and denial of passion; staying upright when family, religion, and the hardscrabble life of sheep farming on a Scottish island beat you down. Some books just get to you. This one gets to me."

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Deep Sky Astrophotography Processing class (class 1 of 3)
description: Have you ever admired amazing deep sky astrophotography images and wondered if you could ever create similar images?  Now you can!   With raw data provided from the telescopes at the Robert Ferguson Observatory, in this class series of three sessions you will have the opportunity to learn how to process and edit your own beautiful deep sky images. Please note, this workshop is meant as a 3-class series. It is highly recommended to purchase tickets for all three days.Please note, this is a virtual class. A Zoom link will be sent to participants prior to the class. What you will learn in this class:- The fundamentals of Deep Sky Astrophotography- An overview of image capture techniques (a dedicated, hands-on class on Deep sky image capture using your own equipment will be held later in Spring 2025)- Robert Ferguson Observatory Image capture techniques - how we captured the data that will be used in this class.- An overview of image processing techniques- An introduction to Siril, a free and open-source Astronomical Image Processing Program- A hands-on session where you will process data collected at the Robert Ferguson Observatory - A wrap-up session where you will have the opportunity to share and discuss your images with other class attendees Class Prerequisites:- A computer newer than 5-years old (the newer the better), loaded with the latest operating system- At least 8MB of RAM (more is better)- At least 50GB of free disk space (preferably a solid-state disk drive.  More storage is better)- Familiarity with creating directories, moving files between folders, setting folder and file permissions, and accessing cloud drives.Get more information and purchase tickets at rfo.simpletix.com.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Focus Night: Jupiter
location: Robert Ferguson Observatory, 2605 Adobe Canyon Rd, Kenwood, CA 95452, USA
description: Have you ever wondered what's really out there in the night sky? Wished you could zoom in on cosmic marvels? What if you had a handful of astronomers at your elbow, showing the way, answering your questions in plain language? That's a Focus Night at the Robert Ferguson Observatory! These are small groups so you get plenty of scope time, and a chance to focus on Jupiter, the largest planet in our solar system! Learn about the Great Red Spot, the four Galilean moons, missions to Jupiter, and much more. If you've never seen Jupiter in a telescope, you're missing out on the thrill of a lifetime. But that's not all! Other spectacles of the night sky, including nebulae and galaxies, also await. The program starts promptly at 7:00 PM. Afterward, weather permitting, we will move to two of  RFO's telescopes (an 8" refractor and a 40" reflector) for a deeper exploration. Sales are limited to 40 guests so we can provide a more personal experience. You'll have plenty of time at the telescope eyepieces, and as always, the observatory will be staffed by knowledgeable and enthusiastic volunteers eager to show you the night sights, and answer any questions you may have.The program begins promptly at 7:00 pm. Allow generous time to arrive and park.Alternate date in case of bad weather is March 13, 2026.$50.00 per adult, $45.00 for seniors (62+) and students, and $40 for members. Cost includes the Sugarloaf Ridge State Park parking fee. You MUST have a ticket to attend this event.  Attendance is limited. Please note that tickets are non-refundable and cannot be used for future events. RFO is operated by the Valley of the Moon Observatory Association, a 501(3)(c) nonprofit organization, and all of the proceeds will go towards maintaining this beloved Sonoma county institution.Please visit www.rfo.simpletix.com for important information and to buy tickets. Seating is limited and you MUST have a ticket to attend this event; tickets will not be sold at the door.

title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Deep Sky Astrophotography Processing class (class 2 of 3)
description: Have you ever admired amazing deep sky astrophotography images and wondered if you could ever create similar images?  Now you can!   With raw data provided from the telescopes at the Robert Ferguson Observatory, in this class series of three sessions you will have the opportunity to learn how to process and edit your own beautiful deep sky images. Please note, this workshop is meant as a 3-class series. title: Standing in Her Power: Portraits Beyond the Colonial Frame
description: Spanning ages 20 to 81, the women featured in the exhibition represent a diversity of lives, identities and experiences that challenge any single representation of Indigenous womanhood. They are land defenders, language keepers, dancers, bead workers, mothers, daughters and artists, each with their own relationship to culture, community, land and identity.  Julian Cook, an SRJC anthropology student and co-creator of the project, conceived the exhibition shortly after she began working at the SRJC Multicultural Museum. While cataloging the museum's book collection, Cook came across Edward S. Curtis: The Women, a collection of photographs that, despite being shaped by romanticized notions of Native peoples as a "vanishing race," also captured the dignity and everyday lives of Native women.  "I don't want to replace one narrow image of Native womanhood with another," Cook explains. "I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

description: Join us for an unforgettable evening of stargazing, exploration, and cozy treats at Cosmos and Cocoa! This event brings together the wonders of the cosmos with a warm cup of cocoa.Kick off the night with a short, guided hike along a portion our captivating Planet Walk, where you'll encounter scale models of many of our solar system’s planets, each with its own unique story. Experts will be on hand to answer questions and guide you through the night sky’s best features.And of course, stay warm with complimentary cups of rich cocoa as you marvel at the universe above. Whether you're an avid stargazer or a curious beginner, Cosmos and Cocoa promises an evening filled with wonder and warmth.No prior experience necessary, and all ages are welcome. Dress warmly and bring a flashlight with a red light setting (no white light allowed). Red light flashlights will also be available for purchase. Register at rfo.simpletix.com.

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

"I want to challenge the idea that there is any single look of a Native woman, and to give these women the opportunity to decide for themselves how they wanted to be seen."  To bring that vision to life, the museum collaborated with San Francisco-based Mexican American photographer Alexa "LexMex" Treviño (https://www.lexmexart.com/about), whose work explores cultural identity, community and representation through portraiture. Her previous projects include Corazón de la Misión, a series of monumental public portraits honoring members of San Francisco's Latinx community.  Each woman featured in Standing in Her Power exercised complete creative control over her portrait, choosing how to present herself rather than conforming to someone else's expectations of what a Native woman should look like. The accompanying stories offer a more personal perspective on the connections between identity, culture, ancestry, and community.This project is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.  For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum website (https://museum.santarosa.edu/event/standing-her-power-portraits-beyond-colonial-frame).

title: Good People by Patmeena Sabit [option 1]
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
\* [Tommy Orange, NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/03/books/review/good-people-patmeena-sabit.html?unlocked_article_code=1.NFE.WCg_.9RX0svI7dnp6&smid=url-share): "Gorgeous and powerful debut novel... *Good People* borrows freely from the language of cinema and television and even social media, in which interviewees essentially talk directly to the reader, as if into a camera... The story is told through a polyphony of outsiders — neighbors, business associates, schoolteachers, reporters. It is a chorus of “good people” whose observations, colored by their own smallness and prejudices, slowly assemble a portrait of a family they never truly knew... Sabit also speaks voluminously about the impossible burden and loneliness of the second-generation experience. There is a profound sadness in the way the 'good people' here settle on a version of truth that satisfies their own worldview.

\* Ed: "18 year old Afghan-American Zorah is dead. Was it an accident or an honor killing? A Greek chorus of other Afghans in a posh Virginia suburb, neighbors, journalists, an anti-violence against women NGO, a defense attorney all speak -- but we do not hear directly from the principals nor is there an omniscient narrator in this finely crafted polyphonic 400 pager that reads very fast because of the short statements from the chorus members. It was a vibrant read. I strongly recommend it."

\* Lucinda: "This book is a stunner. I could not put it down and if you don’t believe me, Ann Patchett says it’s a 'thrilling tour de force of a novel.' I was so impressed with Sabit’s ability to tell the story through so many voices but never lose the thread of the narrative. In her Author’s Note she says she wanted to tell a story of not the fact, but the possibility of an 'honor crime'” and to tell it at a deeper level with the voices that are largely silent or unsought. It’s a bold book and skillfully written. This is her first published novel that took her ten years to complete. I’d highly recommend it."

\* Debra: "Good People is a stunner. It’s part mystery, part documentary-style oral history, a sharp critique of the media, and a deep look at the immigrant experience—all while constantly forcing you to ask where the line is between actual fact and hearsay. I recommend not reading too much about the book before you start the book."

\* Joan: "My ears and mind were glued to the audiobook, and two weeks later, I think about daily. Unusual format: A family is at the center of the story, but it's told by many voices who know or interact or investigate the family - never the family itself. I was both emotionally involved and intellectually sparked."

See reviews, resources, and more comments on our Discord.

title: THIRSTY THURSDAY New Member Social for Sonoma County Women's Wine Club
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
This is our regular club meeting, held on the last Thursday of every month except for holidays and we are super excited! Come join us at 4th Street Cellars in downtown Santa Rosa. They have generously offered to host our monthly THIRSTY THURSDAY social for us.

If you are new to the area, or just looking to get out of the house and make new friends, this is the place for you. Welcoming to ALL new and (ahem, old) members.

Wine is purchased by the glass for a set fee of $13/$14 per glass with the variety of white, rosé, and red wines offered through 4th Street Cellars which includes tip. Fees are collected at the venue by Co-organizer Daima Phipps via cash, Venmo, or Paypal. You are welcome to purchase wine separately if you choose. Starting in 2026, we ask that every attending member pay a $2 "slush" fund fee per event so that we can build up our funds for club-related expenses, which can be paid by Venmo or cash.

There is no food offered, but you are welcome to bring an appetizer or snack to share with the group, and many ladies do. We will have time to socialize while tasting in the room upstairs to the left or the outside patio if the weather is nice.

The space has a 25 person attendee limit, but the list is open to 40 to eliminate a waitlist, and guests are welcome! Please RSVP below only if you are able to make it, we have an attendance policy: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

See you there, ready to kickoff!

title: Good People by Patmeena Sabit [option 2]
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
\* [Tommy Orange, NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/03/books/review/good-people-patmeena-sabit.html?unlocked_article_code=1.NFE.WCg_.9RX0svI7dnp6&smid=url-share): "Gorgeous and powerful debut novel... *Good People* borrows freely from the language of cinema and television and even social media, in which interviewees essentially talk directly to the reader, as if into a camera... The story is told through a polyphony of outsiders — neighbors, business associates, schoolteachers, reporters. It is a chorus of “good people” whose observations, colored by their own smallness and prejudices, slowly assemble a portrait of a family they never truly knew... Sabit also speaks voluminously about the impossible burden and loneliness of the second-generation experience. There is a profound sadness in the way the 'good people' here settle on a version of truth that satisfies their own worldview.

\* Ed: "18 year old Afghan-American Zorah is dead. Was it an accident or an honor killing? A Greek chorus of other Afghans in a posh Virginia suburb, neighbors, journalists, an anti-violence against women NGO, a defense attorney all speak -- but we do not hear directly from the principals nor is there an omniscient narrator in this finely crafted polyphonic 400 pager that reads very fast because of the short statements from the chorus members. It was a vibrant read. I strongly recommend it."

\* Lucinda: "This book is a stunner. I could not put it down and if you don’t believe me, Ann Patchett says it’s a 'thrilling tour de force of a novel.' I was so impressed with Sabit’s ability to tell the story through so many voices but never lose the thread of the narrative. In her Author’s Note she says she wanted to tell a story of not the fact, but the possibility of an 'honor crime'” and to tell it at a deeper level with the voices that are largely silent or unsought. It’s a bold book and skillfully written. This is her first published novel that took her ten years to complete. I’d highly recommend it."

\* Debra: "Good People is a stunner. It’s part mystery, part documentary-style oral history, a sharp critique of the media, and a deep look at the immigrant experience—all while constantly forcing you to ask where the line is between actual fact and hearsay. I recommend not reading too much about the book before you start the book."

\* Joan: "My ears and mind were glued to the audiobook, and two weeks later, I think about daily. Unusual format: A family is at the center of the story, but it's told by many voices who know or interact or investigate the family - never the family itself. I was both emotionally involved and intellectually sparked."

See reviews, resources, and more comments on our Discord.

title: THIRSTY THURSDAY New Member Social for Sonoma County Women's Wine Club
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
This is our regular club meeting, held on the last Thursday of every month except for holidays and we are super excited! Come join us at 4th Street Cellars in downtown Santa Rosa. They have generously offered to host our monthly THIRSTY THURSDAY social for us.

If you are new to the area, or just looking to get out of the house and make new friends, this is the place for you. Welcoming to ALL new and (ahem, old) members.

Wine is purchased by the glass for a set fee of $13/$14 per glass with the variety of white, rosé, and red wines offered through 4th Street Cellars which includes tip. Fees are collected at the venue by Co-organizer Daima Phipps via cash, Venmo, or Paypal. You are welcome to purchase wine separately if you choose. Starting in 2026, we ask that every attending member pay a $2 "slush" fund fee per event so that we can build up our funds for club-related expenses, which can be paid by Venmo or cash.

There is no food offered, but you are welcome to bring an appetizer or snack to share with the group, and many ladies do. We will have time to socialize while tasting in the room upstairs to the left or the outside patio if the weather is nice.

The space has a 25 person attendee limit, but the list is open to 40 to eliminate a waitlist, and guests are welcome! Please RSVP below only if you are able to make it, we have an attendance policy: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

See you there, ready to kickoff!

Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

title: THIRSTY THURSDAY New Member Social for Sonoma County Women's Wine Club
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
This is our regular club meeting, held on the last Thursday of every month except for holidays and we are super excited! Come join us at 4th Street Cellars in downtown Santa Rosa. They have generously offered to host our monthly THIRSTY THURSDAY social for us.

If you are new to the area, or just looking to get out of the house and make new friends, this is the place for you. Welcoming to ALL new and (ahem, old) members.

Wine is purchased by the glass for a set fee of $13/$14 per glass with the variety of white, rosé, and red wines offered through 4th Street Cellars which includes tip. Fees are collected at the venue by Co-organizer Daima Phipps via cash, Venmo, or Paypal. You are welcome to purchase wine separately if you choose. Starting in 2026, we ask that every attending member pay a $2 "slush" fund fee per event so that we can build up our funds for club-related expenses, which can be paid by Venmo or cash.

There is no food offered, but you are welcome to bring an appetizer or snack to share with the group, and many ladies do. We will have time to socialize while tasting in the room upstairs to the left or the outside patio if the weather is nice.

The space has a 25 person attendee limit, but the list is open to 40 to eliminate a waitlist, and guests are welcome! Please RSVP below only if you are able to make it, we have an attendance policy: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

See you there, ready to kickoff!

title: THIRSTY THURSDAY New Member Social for Sonoma County Women's Wine Club
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
This is our regular club meeting, held on the last Thursday of every month except for holidays and we are super excited! Come join us at 4th Street Cellars in downtown Santa Rosa. They have generously offered to host our monthly THIRSTY THURSDAY social for us.

If you are new to the area, or just looking to get out of the house and make new friends, this is the place for you. Welcoming to ALL new and (ahem, old) members.

Wine is purchased by the glass for a set fee of $13/$14 per glass with the variety of white, rosé, and red wines offered through 4th Street Cellars which includes tip. Fees are collected at the venue by Co-organizer Daima Phipps via cash, Venmo, or Paypal. You are welcome to purchase wine separately if you choose. Starting in 2026, we ask that every attending member pay a $2 "slush" fund fee per event so that we can build up our funds for club-related expenses, which can be paid by Venmo or cash.

There is no food offered, but you are welcome to bring an appetizer or snack to share with the group, and many ladies do. We will have time to socialize while tasting in the room upstairs to the left or the outside patio if the weather is nice.

The space has a 25 person attendee limit, but the list is open to 40 to eliminate a waitlist, and guests are welcome! Please RSVP below only if you are able to make it, we have an attendance policy: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

See you there, ready to kickoff!

description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

title: THIRSTY THURSDAY New Member Social for Sonoma County Women's Wine Club
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
This is our regular club meeting, held on the last Thursday of every month except for holidays and we are super excited! Come join us at 4th Street Cellars in downtown Santa Rosa. They have generously offered to host our monthly THIRSTY THURSDAY social for us.

If you are new to the area, or just looking to get out of the house and make new friends, this is the place for you. Welcoming to ALL new and (ahem, old) members.

Wine is purchased by the glass for a set fee of $13/$14 per glass with the variety of white, rosé, and red wines offered through 4th Street Cellars which includes tip. Fees are collected at the venue by Co-organizer Daima Phipps via cash, Venmo, or Paypal. You are welcome to purchase wine separately if you choose. Starting in 2026, we ask that every attending member pay a $2 "slush" fund fee per event so that we can build up our funds for club-related expenses, which can be paid by Venmo or cash.

There is no food offered, but you are welcome to bring an appetizer or snack to share with the group, and many ladies do. We will have time to socialize while tasting in the room upstairs to the left or the outside patio if the weather is nice.

The space has a 25 person attendee limit, but the list is open to 40 to eliminate a waitlist, and guests are welcome! Please RSVP below only if you are able to make it, we have an attendance policy: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

See you there, ready to kickoff!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.

  * Capturing shapes and light in your work

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

title: Santa Rosa Game Night
description:
Santa Rosa Game Night
An evening of board games and cards preceded by pot luck snacks. Bring a game, play what is there, learn a new game, socialize, eat! Members are welcoming and friendly, ready to teach new people how to play. Please, no Crimes against Humanity.
We ask for a $2 donation to cover the cost.

Game Night is the third Saturday of every month unless otherwise noted. If cancelled, you will receive an email notice. Lately we have a lot of no shows. Please take your reservation seriously and give us advance notice if you cannot attend.
It is a good idea to arrive at 6:00.

title: Take the art of Still Life to new places
location: Rileystreet Art Supply, 103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Thursdays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 11:30am - 1:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

description:
Instructor: Ann Marie Torrez
On-going, Thursdays
2:00PM-4:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$35.00 Per Class

Join Ann Torrez and learn a few different ways to achieve instant gratification quickly in your drawings and get to the fun part of creating!

Ann will introduce you to a variety of drawing materials and teach you how to use them. You can also expect to explore a variety of different papers, and materials that will aid in transferring your sketch to a more refined, complete piece of artwork.

You can expect a mix of practical tips, upbeat encouragement and a little entertainment that will help you break through mental barriers and hesitations!


To register, please email Ann at: annde_2@yahoo.com mailto:annde_2@yahoo.com or call/ text her at 707-548-6499

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

description:

This Figure drawing session provides artists with the opportunity to practice drawing techniques with a live model in different poses. This process helps the artist capture the essence of the human body’s posture, texture, and movement.

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.

  * Capturing shapes and light in your work

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

title: Santa Rosa Game Night
description:
Santa Rosa Game Night
An evening of board games and cards preceded by pot luck snacks. Bring a game, play what is there, learn a new game, socialize, eat! Members are welcoming and friendly, ready to teach new people how to play. Please, no Crimes against Humanity.
We ask for a $2 donation to cover the cost.

Game Night is the third Saturday of every month unless otherwise noted. If cancelled, you will receive an email notice. Lately we have a lot of no shows. Please take your reservation seriously and give us advance notice if you cannot attend.
It is a good idea to arrive at 6:00.

title: Take the art of Still Life to new places
location: Rileystreet Art Supply, 103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Thursdays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 11:30am - 1:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

description:
Instructor: Ann Marie Torrez
On-going, Thursdays
2:00PM-4:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$35.00 Per Class

Join Ann Torrez and learn a few different ways to achieve instant gratification quickly in your drawings and get to the fun part of creating!

Ann will introduce you to a variety of drawing materials and teach you how to use them. You can also expect to explore a variety of different papers, and materials that will aid in transferring your sketch to a more refined, complete piece of artwork.

You can expect a mix of practical tips, upbeat encouragement and a little entertainment that will help you break through mental barriers and hesitations!


To register, please email Ann at: annde_2@yahoo.com mailto:annde_2@yahoo.com or call/ text her at 707-548-6499

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

description:

This Figure drawing session provides artists with the opportunity to practice drawing techniques with a live model in different poses. This process helps the artist capture the essence of the human body’s posture, texture, and movement.
